61.s:
brahmovāca
devān pitṝṃs tathā cānyān saṃtarpyācamya vāgyataḥ
hastamātraṃ catuṣkoṇaṃ caturdvāraṃ suśobhanam //
61.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
देवान् पितॄंस् तथा चान्यान् संतर्प्याचम्य वाग्यतः
हस्तमात्रं चतुष्कोणं चतुर्द्वारं सुशोभनम् ॥
61.m: Brahmā said: / Having satiated the gods, ancestors, and others, having sipped water, restrained in speech, / [one should draw] a beautiful square four-portal city, one cubit in measure,

61.s:
puraṃ vilikhya bho viprās tīre tasya mahodadheḥ
madhye tatra likhet padmam aṣṭapattraṃ sakarṇikam //
61.d:
पुरं विलिख्य भो विप्रास् तीरे तस्य महोदधेः
मध्ये तत्र लिखेत् पद्मम् अष्टपत्त्रं सकर्णिकम् ॥
61.m: having drawn it, O brahmins, on the shore of that great ocean; / there in the center one should draw an eight-petaled lotus with a pericarp.

61.s:
evaṃ maṇḍalam ālikhya pūjayet tatra bho dvijāḥ
aṣṭākṣaravidhānena nārāyaṇam ajaṃ vibhum //
61.d:
एवं मण्डलम् आलिख्य पूजयेत् तत्र भो द्विजाः
अष्टाक्षरविधानेन नारायणम् अजं विभुम् ॥
61.m: Having thus drawn the maṇḍala, one should worship there, O twice-born, / through the rite of the eight-syllable [mantra], the unborn, all-pervading Nārāyaṇa.

61.s:
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi kāyaśodhanam uttamam
akāraṃ hṛdaye dhyātvā cakrarekhāsamanvitam //
61.d:
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि कायशोधनम् उत्तमम्
अकारं हृदये ध्यात्वा चक्ररेखासमन्वितम् ॥
61.m: Next, I shall explain the supreme purification of the body: / meditating in the heart upon the letter 'a', endowed with the line of a discus,

61.s:
jvalantaṃ triśikhaṃ caiva dahantaṃ pāpanāśanam
candramaṇḍalamadhyasthaṃ rākāraṃ mūrdhni cintayet //
61.d:
ज्वलन्तं त्रिशिखं चैव दहन्तं पापनाशनम्
चन्द्रमण्डलमध्यस्थं राकारं मूर्ध्नि चिन्तयेत् ॥
61.m: blazing, three-crested, burning, destroying sin; / one should contemplate the letter 'ra' upon the head, situated within the orb of the moon,

61.s:
śuklavarṇaṃ pravarṣantam amṛtaṃ plāvayan mahīm
evaṃ nirdhūtapāpas tu divyadehas tato bhavet //
61.d:
शुक्लवर्णं प्रवर्षन्तम् अमृतं प्लावयन् महीम्
एवं निर्धूतपापस् तु दिव्यदेहस् ततो भवेत् ॥
61.m: white-colored, showering nectar, flooding the earth. / Having thus washed away his sins, one then becomes possessed of a divine body.

61.s:
aṣṭākṣaraṃ tato mantraṃ nyased evātmano budhaḥ
vāmapādaṃ samārabhya kramaśaś caiva vinyaset //
61.d:
अष्टाक्षरं ततो मन्त्रं न्यसेद् एवात्मनो बुधः
वामपादं समारभ्य क्रमशश् चैव विन्यसेत् ॥
61.m: The wise man should then impose the eight-syllable mantra upon himself; / beginning from the left foot, he should deposit it in proper order.

61.s:
pañcāṅgaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ caiva caturvyūhaṃ tathaiva ca
karaśuddhiṃ prakurvīta mūlamantreṇa sādhakaḥ //
61.d:
पञ्चाङ्गं वैष्णवं चैव चतुर्व्यूहं तथैव च
करशुद्धिं प्रकुर्वीत मूलमन्त्रेण साधकः ॥
61.m: The five-limbed [nyāsa], that of Viṣṇu, and likewise that of the four emanations: / the practitioner should perform the purification of hands with the root-mantra.

61.s:
ekaikaṃ caiva varṇaṃ tu aṅgulīṣu pṛthak pṛthak
oṃkāraṃ pṛthivīṃ śuklāṃ vāmapāde tu vinyaset //
61.d:
एकैकं चैव वर्णं तु अङ्गुलीषु पृथक् पृथक्
ओंकारं पृथिवीं शुक्लां वामपादे तु विन्यसेत् ॥
61.m: One letter at a time, separately on the fingers: / one should place the syllable 'oṃ', [representing] the white earth, on the left foot;

61.s:
nakāraḥ śāṃbhavaḥ śyāmo dakṣiṇe tu vyavasthitaḥ
mokāraṃ kālam evāhur vāmakaṭyāṃ nidhāpayet //
61.d:
नकारः शांभवः श्यामो दक्षिणे तु व्यवस्थितः
मोकारं कालम् एवाहुर् वामकट्यां निधापयेत् ॥
61.m: the syllable 'na', connected with Śambhu, dark, is placed on the right [foot]; / they say the syllable 'mo' is time: one should place it on the left hip;

61.s:
nākāraḥ sarvabījaṃ tu dakṣiṇasyāṃ vyavasthitaḥ
rākāras teja ity āhur nābhideśe vyavasthitaḥ //
61.d:
नाकारः सर्वबीजं तु दक्षिणस्यां व्यवस्थितः
राकारस् तेज इत्य् आहुर् नाभिदेशे व्यवस्थितः ॥
61.m: the syllable 'nā', the universal seed, is situated on the right [hip]; / they say the syllable 'rā' is fire: it is situated in the region of the navel;

61.s:
vāyavyo 'yaṃ yakāras tu vāmaskandhe samāśritaḥ
ṇākāraḥ sarvago jñeyo dakṣiṇāṃse vyavasthitaḥ
yakāro 'yaṃ śirasthaś ca yatra lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ //
61.d:
वायव्यो ऽयं यकारस् तु वामस्कन्धे समाश्रितः
णाकारः सर्वगो ज्ञेयो दक्षिणांसे व्यवस्थितः
यकारो ऽयं शिरस्थश् च यत्र लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः ॥
61.m: this syllable 'ya' belongs to the wind and rests on the left shoulder; / the syllable 'ṇa' is known as all-pervading and is placed on the right shoulder; / and this syllable 'ya' rests on the head, where the worlds are established.

61.s: oṃ viṣṇave namaḥ śiraḥ oṃ jvalanāya namaḥ śikhā | oṃ viṣṇave namaḥ kavacam oṃ viṣṇave namaḥ sphuraṇaṃ diśobandhāya | oṃ huṃphaḍastram oṃ śirasi śuklo vāsudeva iti | oṃ āṃ lalāṭe raktaḥ saṃkarṣaṇo garutmān vahnis teja āditya iti | oṃ āṃ grīvāyāṃ pītaḥ pradyumno vāyumegha iti | oṃ āṃ hṛdaye kṛṣṇo 'niruddhaḥ sarvaśaktisamanvita iti | evaṃ caturvyūham ātmānaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ karma samācaret ||
61.d: ओं विष्णवे नमः शिरः ओं ज्वलनाय नमः शिखा । ओं विष्णवे नमः कवचम् ओं विष्णवे नमः स्फुरणं दिशोबन्धाय । ओं हुंफडस्त्रम् ओं शिरसि शुक्लो वासुदेव इति । ओं आं ललाटे रक्तः संकर्षणो गरुत्मान् वह्निस् तेज आदित्य इति । ओं आं ग्रीवायां पीतः प्रद्युम्नो वायुमेघ इति । ओं आं हृदये कृष्णो ऽनिरुद्धः सर्वशक्तिसमन्वित इति । एवं चतुर्व्यूहम् आत्मानं कृत्वा ततः कर्म समाचरेत् ॥
61.m: 'Oṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu', the head; 'Oṃ, obeisance to the blazing one', the crest; 'Oṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu', the armor; 'Oṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu', the flash for binding the directions; 'Oṃ huṃ phaṭ', the weapon; 'Oṃ, white Vāsudeva on the head'; 'Oṃ āṃ, red Saṃkarṣaṇa on the forehead, Garuḍa, fire, splendor, the sun'; 'Oṃ āṃ, yellow Pradyumna at the throat, wind, cloud'; 'Oṃ āṃ, black Aniruddha in the heart, endowed with all powers'. Having thus made himself into the four emanations, he should then undertake the rite.

61.s:
mamāgre 'vasthito viṣṇuḥ pṛṣṭhataś cāpi keśavaḥ
govindo dakṣiṇe pārśve vāme tu madhusūdanaḥ //
61.d:
ममाग्रे ऽवस्थितो विष्णुः पृष्ठतश् चापि केशवः
गोविन्दो दक्षिणे पार्श्वे वामे तु मधुसूदनः ॥
61.m: Viṣṇu stands before me, and Keśava behind; / Govinda is at my right side, and Madhusūdana at my left;

61.s:
upariṣṭāt tu vaikuṇṭho vārāhaḥ pṛthivītale
avāntaradiśo yās tu tāsu sarvāsu mādhavaḥ //
61.d:
उपरिष्टात् तु वैकुण्ठो वाराहः पृथिवीतले
अवान्तरदिशो यास् तु तासु सर्वासु माधवः ॥
61.m: Vaikuṇṭha is above, the Boar is on the surface of the earth; / and Mādhava is present in all the intermediate directions.

61.s:
gacchatas tiṣṭhato vāpi jāgrataḥ svapato 'pi vā
narasiṃhakṛtā guptir vāsudevamayo hy aham //
61.d:
गच्छतस् तिष्ठतो वापि जाग्रतः स्वपतो ऽपि वा
नरसिंहकृता गुप्तिर् वासुदेवमयो ह्य् अहम् ॥
61.m: Whether walking or standing, waking or sleeping, / protection is made by Narasiṃha; indeed, I consist of Vāsudeva.

61.s:
evaṃ viṣṇumayo bhūtvā tataḥ karma samārabhet
yathā dehe tathā deve sarvatattvāni yojayet //
61.d:
एवं विष्णुमयो भूत्वा ततः कर्म समारभेत्
यथा देहे तथा देवे सर्वतत्त्वानि योजयेत् ॥
61.m: Having thus become composed of Viṣṇu, one should then begin the rite: / as in the body, so in the deity one should join all the principles of reality.

61.s:
tataś caiva prakurvīta prokṣaṇaṃ praṇavena tu
phaṭkārāntaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ sarvavighnaharaṃ śubham //
61.d:
ततश् चैव प्रकुर्वीत प्रोक्षणं प्रणवेन तु
फट्कारान्तं समुद्दिष्टं सर्वविघ्नहरं शुभम् ॥
61.m: And then one should perform sprinkling with the praṇava, / taught as ending with the sound 'phaṭ', which removes all obstacles and is auspicious.

61.s:
tatrārkacandravahnīnāṃ maṇḍalāni vicintayet
padmamadhye nyased viṣṇuṃ pavanasyāmbarasya ca //
61.d:
तत्रार्कचन्द्रवह्नीनां मण्डलानि विचिन्तयेत्
पद्ममध्ये न्यसेद् विष्णुं पवनस्याम्बरस्य च ॥
61.m: There one should contemplate the orbs of the sun, moon, and fire; / in the center of the lotus one should place Viṣṇu, and those of the wind and space.

61.s:
tato vicintya hṛdaya oṃkāraṃ jyotīrūpiṇam
karṇikāyāṃ samāsīnaṃ jyotīrūpaṃ sanātanam //
61.d:
ततो विचिन्त्य हृदय ओंकारं ज्योतीरूपिणम्
कर्णिकायां समासीनं ज्योतीरूपं सनातनम् ॥
61.m: Then having contemplated in the heart the syllable 'oṃ', whose form is light, / seated in the pericarp, the eternal one whose form is light,

61.s:
aṣṭākṣaraṃ tato mantraṃ vinyasec ca yathākramam
tena vyastasamastena pūjanaṃ paramaṃ smṛtam //
61.d:
अष्टाक्षरं ततो मन्त्रं विन्यसेच् च यथाक्रमम्
तेन व्यस्तसमस्तेन पूजनं परमं स्मृतम् ॥
61.m: one should then deposit the eight-syllable mantra in proper order; / worship done with it, divided and combined, is recorded as supreme.

61.s:
dvādaśākṣaramantreṇa yajed devaṃ sanātanam
tato 'vadhārya hṛdaye karṇikāyāṃ bahir nyaset //
61.d:
द्वादशाक्षरमन्त्रेण यजेद् देवं सनातनम्
ततो ऽवधार्य हृदये कर्णिकायां बहिर् न्यसेत् ॥
61.m: One should worship the eternal deity with the twelve-syllable mantra; / then, having grasped him in the heart, one should place him externally on the pericarp.

61.s:
caturbhujaṃ mahāsattvaṃ sūryakoṭisamaprabham
cintayitvā mahāyogaṃ jyotīrūpaṃ sanātanam
tataś cāvāhayen mantraṃ krameṇācintya mānase //
61.d:
चतुर्भुजं महासत्त्वं सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभम्
चिन्तयित्वा महायोगं ज्योतीरूपं सनातनम्
ततश् चावाहयेन् मन्त्रं क्रमेणाचिन्त्य मानसे ॥
61.m: Having contemplated the four-armed one of great being, equal in radiance to ten million suns, / of great yoga, the eternal one whose form is light, / one should then invoke the mantra in the mind, meditating [upon him] in proper order.

61.s:
āvāhanamantraḥ: mīnarūpo varāhaś ca narasiṃho 'tha vāmanaḥ | āyātu devo varado mama nārāyaṇo 'grataḥ ||
oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya namaḥ ||
61.d:
आवाहनमन्त्रः: मीनरूपो वराहश् च नरसिंहो ऽथ वामनः । आयातु देवो वरदो मम नारायणो ऽग्रतः ॥
ओं नमो नारायणाय नमः ॥
61.m: Invocation mantra: 'The Fish-form, the Boar, Narasiṃha, and Vāmana— / may the boon-giving god Nārāyaṇa come before me! / Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, obeisance!'

61.s:
karṇikāyāṃ supīṭhe 'tra padmakalpitam āsanam
sarvasattvahitārthāya tiṣṭha tvaṃ madhusūdana //
oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya namaḥ ||
61.d:
कर्णिकायां सुपीठे ऽत्र पद्मकल्पितम् आसनम्
सर्वसत्त्वहितार्थाय तिष्ठ त्वं मधुसूदन ॥
ओं नमो नारायणाय नमः ॥
61.m: 'Here upon the auspicious seat on the pericarp, the seat fashioned as a lotus, / stand for the sake of the welfare of all beings, O Madhusūdana! / Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, obeisance!'

61.s: arghamantraḥ: oṃ trailokyapatīnāṃ pataye devadevāya hṛṣīkeśāya viṣṇave namaḥ | oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya namaḥ ||
61.d: अर्घमन्त्रः: ओं त्रैलोक्यपतीनां पतये देवदेवाय हृषीकेशाय विष्णवे नमः । ओं नमो नारायणाय नमः ॥
61.m: Water-offering mantra: 'Oṃ, obeisance to the lord of the lords of the three worlds, to the god of gods, to Hṛṣīkeśa, to Viṣṇu! / Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, obeisance!'

61.s:
oṃ pādyaṃ pādayor deva padmanābha sanātana
viṣṇo kamalapattrākṣa gṛhāṇa madhusūdana //
oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya namaḥ ||
61.d:
ओं पाद्यं पादयोर् देव पद्मनाभ सनातन
विष्णो कमलपत्त्राक्ष गृहाण मधुसूदन ॥
ओं नमो नारायणाय नमः ॥
61.m: 'Oṃ, this water for the feet is for your feet, O god, lotus-navelled, eternal one! / O Viṣṇu with eyes like lotus petals, accept it, O Madhusūdana! / Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, obeisance!'

61.s:
madhuparkaṃ mahādeva brahmādyaiḥ kalpitaṃ tava
mayā niveditaṃ bhaktyā gṛhāṇa puruṣottama //
oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya namaḥ ||
61.d:
मधुपर्कं महादेव ब्रह्माद्यैः कल्पितं तव
मया निवेदितं भक्त्या गृहाण पुरुषोत्तम ॥
ओं नमो नारायणाय नमः ॥
61.m: 'The honey-mixture, O great god, fashioned for you by Brahmā and the others, / is offered by me with devotion; accept it, O Puruṣottama! / Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, obeisance!'

61.s:
ācamanīyamantraḥ
mandākinyāḥ sitaṃ vāri sarvapāpaharaṃ śivam
gṛhāṇācamanīyaṃ tvaṃ mayā bhaktyā niveditam //
oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya namaḥ ||
61.d:
आचमनीयमन्त्रः
मन्दाकिन्याः सितं वारि सर्वपापहरं शिवम्
गृहाणाचमनीयं त्वं मया भक्त्या निवेदितम् ॥
ओं नमो नारायणाय नमः ॥
61.m: Sipping-water mantra: / 'The white, auspicious water of the Mandākinī, removing all sins— / accept this sipping water offered by me with devotion! / Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, obeisance!'

61.s:
snānamantraḥ
tvam āpaḥ pṛthivī caiva jyotis tvaṃ vāyur eva ca
lokeśa vṛttimātreṇa vāriṇā snāpayāmy aham //
oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya namaḥ ||
61.d:
स्नानमन्त्रः
त्वम् आपः पृथिवी चैव ज्योतिस् त्वं वायुर् एव च
लोकेश वृत्तिमात्रेण वारिणा स्नापयाम्य् अहम् ॥
ओं नमो नारायणाय नमः ॥
61.m: Bathing mantra: / 'You are the waters, the earth, the light, and the wind; / O lord of the world, I bathe you merely as an observance with water! / Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, obeisance!'

61.s:
vastramantraḥ
devatattvasamāyukta yajñavarṇasamanvita
svarṇavarṇaprabhe deva vāsasī tava keśava //
oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya namaḥ ||
61.d:
वस्त्रमन्त्रः
देवतत्त्वसमायुक्त यज्ञवर्णसमन्वित
स्वर्णवर्णप्रभे देव वाससी तव केशव ॥
ओं नमो नारायणाय नमः ॥
61.m: Garment mantra: / 'Endowed with divine reality, possessed of the sacrificial color, / radiant with a golden color, O god, these two garments are yours, O Keśava! / Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, obeisance!'

61.s:
vilepanamantraḥ
śarīraṃ te na jānāmi ceṣṭāṃ caiva ca keśava
mayā nivedito gandhaḥ pratigṛhya vilipyatām //
oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya namaḥ ||
61.d:
विलेपनमन्त्रः
शरीरं ते न जानामि चेष्टां चैव च केशव
मया निवेदितो गन्धः प्रतिगृह्य विलिप्यताम् ॥
ओं नमो नारायणाय नमः ॥
61.m: Ointment mantra: / 'I do not know your body nor your actions, O Keśava; / accept this fragrant paste offered by me and let it be smeared on! / Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, obeisance!'

61.s:
upavītamantraḥ
ṛgyajuḥsāmamantreṇa trivṛtaṃ padmayoninā
sāvitrīgranthisaṃyuktam upavītaṃ tavārpaye //
oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya namaḥ ||
61.d:
उपवीतमन्त्रः
ऋग्यजुःसाममन्त्रेण त्रिवृतं पद्मयोनिना
सावित्रीग्रन्थिसंयुक्तम् उपवीतं तवार्पये ॥
ओं नमो नारायणाय नमः ॥
61.m: Sacred thread mantra: / 'Threefold through the mantras of the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma, by the lotus-born [Brahmā], / joined with the knot of Sāvitrī, I offer this sacred thread to you! / Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, obeisance!'

61.s:
alaṃkāramantraḥ
divyaratnasamāyukta vahnibhānusamaprabha
gātrāṇi tava śobhantu sālaṃkārāṇi mādhava //
oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya namaḥ ||
oṃ nama iti pratyakṣaraṃ samastena mūlamantreṇa vā pūjayet ||
61.d:
अलंकारमन्त्रः
दिव्यरत्नसमायुक्त वह्निभानुसमप्रभ
गात्राणि तव शोभन्तु सालंकाराणि माधव ॥
ओं नमो नारायणाय नमः ॥
ओं नम इति प्रत्यक्षरं समस्तेन मूलमन्त्रेण वा पूजयेत् ॥
61.m:
Ornament mantra: / 'Endowed with divine jewels, equal in radiance to fire and the sun, / may your limbs shine, adorned with ornaments, O Mādhava! / Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, obeisance!'

One should worship syllable by syllable with 'Oṃ, obeisance', or with the complete root-mantra.

61.s:
dhūpamantraḥ
vanaspatiraso divyo gandhāḍhyaḥ surabhiś ca te
mayā nivedito bhaktyā dhūpo 'yaṃ pratigṛhyatām //
oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya namaḥ ||
61.d:
धूपमन्त्रः
वनस्पतिरसो दिव्यो गन्धाढ्यः सुरभिश् च ते
मया निवेदितो भक्त्या धूपो ऽयं प्रतिगृह्यताम् ॥
ओं नमो नारायणाय नमः ॥
61.m: Incense mantra: / 'The divine sap of trees, rich in fragrance and aromatic to you, / this incense offered by me with devotion, let it be accepted! / Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, obeisance!'

61.s:
dīpamantraḥ
sūryacandrasamo jyotir vidyudagnyos tathaiva ca
tvam eva jyotiṣāṃ deva dīpo 'yaṃ pratigṛhyatām //
oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya namaḥ ||
61.d:
दीपमन्त्रः
सूर्यचन्द्रसमो ज्योतिर् विद्युदग्न्योस् तथैव च
त्वम् एव ज्योतिषां देव दीपो ऽयं प्रतिगृह्यताम् ॥
ओं नमो नारायणाय नमः ॥
61.m: Mantra for the lamp: / Light equal to the sun and moon, and likewise to lightning and fire; / you alone are the god of lights: may this lamp be accepted! / *oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya namaḥ*.

61.s:
naivedyamantraḥ
annaṃ caturvidhaṃ caiva rasaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ samanvitam
mayā niveditaṃ bhaktyā naivedyaṃ tava keśava //
oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya namaḥ ||
61.d:
नैवेद्यमन्त्रः
अन्नं चतुर्विधं चैव रसैः षड्भिः समन्वितम्
मया निवेदितं भक्त्या नैवेद्यं तव केशव ॥
ओं नमो नारायणाय नमः ॥
61.m: Food offering mantra: / 'The four kinds of food endowed with the six flavors, / this food offering is presented by me with devotion to you, O Keśava! / Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇa, obeisance!'

61.s:
pūrve dale vāsudevaṃ yāmye saṃkarṣaṇaṃ nyaset
pradyumnaṃ paścime kuryād aniruddhaṃ tathottare //
61.d:
पूर्वे दले वासुदेवं याम्ये संकर्षणं न्यसेत्
प्रद्युम्नं पश्चिमे कुर्याद् अनिरुद्धं तथोत्तरे ॥
61.m: On the eastern petal one should place Vāsudeva, on the southern Saṃkarṣaṇa, / on the western one should place Pradyumna, and likewise Aniruddha on the northern.

61.s:
vārāhaṃ ca tathāgneye narasiṃhaṃ ca nairṛte
vāyavye mādhavaṃ caiva tathaiśāne trivikramam //
61.d:
वाराहं च तथाग्नेये नरसिंहं च नैरृते
वायव्ये माधवं चैव तथैशाने त्रिविक्रमम् ॥
61.m: And likewise the Boar on the south-eastern, Narasiṃha on the south-western, / Mādhava on the north-western, and likewise Trivikrama on the north-eastern.

61.s:
tathāṣṭākṣaradevasya garuḍaṃ purato nyaset
vāmapārśve tathā cakraṃ śaṅkhaṃ dakṣiṇato nyaset //
61.d:
तथाष्टाक्षरदेवस्य गरुडं पुरतो न्यसेत्
वामपार्श्वे तथा चक्रं शङ्खं दक्षिणतो न्यसेत् ॥
61.m: Likewise, in front of the eight-syllabled deity one should place Garuḍa; / on the left flank one should place the discus, and on the right the conch.

61.s:
tathā mahāgadāṃ caiva nyased devasya dakṣiṇe
tataḥ śārṅgaṃ dhanur vidvān nyased devasya vāmataḥ //
61.d:
तथा महागदां चैव न्यसेद् देवस्य दक्षिणे
ततः शार्ङ्गं धनुर् विद्वान् न्यसेद् देवस्य वामतः ॥
61.m: Likewise, one should place the great mace on the deity's right; / then the wise man should place the bow Śārṅga on the deity's left.

61.s:
dakṣiṇeneṣudhī divye khaḍgaṃ vāme ca vinyaset
śriyaṃ dakṣiṇataḥ sthāpya puṣṭim uttarato nyaset //
61.d:
दक्षिणेनेषुधी दिव्ये खड्गं वामे च विन्यसेत्
श्रियं दक्षिणतः स्थाप्य पुष्टिम् उत्तरतो न्यसेत् ॥
61.m: One should place two divine quivers on the right and a sword on the left; / having established Śrī on the right, one should place Puṣṭi on the north.

61.s:
vanamālāṃ ca puratas tataḥ śrīvatsakaustubhau
vinyased dhṛdayādīni pūrvādiṣu caturdiśam //
61.d:
वनमालां च पुरतस् ततः श्रीवत्सकौस्तुभौ
विन्यसेद् धृदयादीनि पूर्वादिषु चतुर्दिशम् ॥
61.m: And the forest garland in front, and after that the Śrīvatsa and the Kaustubha; / one should place [the limbs] beginning with the heart in the four directions starting with the east.

61.s:
tato 'straṃ devadevasya koṇe caiva tu vinyaset
indram agniṃ yamaṃ caiva nairṛtaṃ varuṇaṃ tathā //
61.d:
ततो ऽस्त्रं देवदेवस्य कोणे चैव तु विन्यसेत्
इन्द्रम् अग्निं यमं चैव नैरृतं वरुणं तथा ॥
61.m: Then one should place the weapon of the god of gods in the corner; / [and] Indra, Agni, Yama, and Nairṛta, and Varuṇa,

61.s:
vāyuṃ dhanadam īśānam anantaṃ brahmaṇā saha
pūjayet tāntrikair mantrair adhaś cordhvaṃ tathaiva ca //
61.d:
वायुं धनदम् ईशानम् अनन्तं ब्रह्मणा सह
पूजयेत् तान्त्रिकैर् मन्त्रैर् अधश् चोर्ध्वं तथैव च ॥
61.m: Vāyu, the giver of wealth, Īśāna, and Ananta together with Brahmā; / one should worship [them] with Tantric mantras below and likewise above.

61.s:
evaṃ saṃpūjya deveśaṃ maṇḍalasthaṃ janārdanam
labhed abhimatān kāmān naro nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ //
61.d:
एवं संपूज्य देवेशं मण्डलस्थं जनार्दनम्
लभेद् अभिमतान् कामान् नरो नास्त्य् अत्र संशयः ॥
61.m: Having thus worshipped the lord of gods, Janārdana situated in the mandala, / a man attains his desired wishes; there is no doubt about this.

61.s:
anenaiva vidhānena maṇḍalasthaṃ janārdanam
pūjitaṃ yaḥ saṃpaśyeta sa viśed viṣṇum avyayam //
61.d:
अनेनैव विधानेन मण्डलस्थं जनार्दनम्
पूजितं यः संपश्येत स विशेद् विष्णुम् अव्ययम् ॥
61.m: Whoever sees Janārdana situated in the mandala, / worshipped according to this very procedure, enters the imperishable Viṣṇu.

61.s:
sakṛd apy arcito yena vidhinānena keśavaḥ
janmamṛtyujarāṃ tīrtvā sa viṣṇoḥ padam āpnuyāt //
61.d:
सकृद् अप्य् अर्चितो येन विधिनानेन केशवः
जन्ममृत्युजरां तीर्त्वा स विष्णोः पदम् आप्नुयात् ॥
61.m: The one by whom Keśava has been worshipped even once according to this procedure, / having crossed over birth, death, and old age, reaches Viṣṇu's abode.

61.s:
yaḥ smaret satataṃ bhaktyā nārāyaṇam atandritaḥ
anvahaṃ tasya vāsāya śvetadvīpaḥ prakalpitaḥ //
61.d:
यः स्मरेत् सततं भक्त्या नारायणम् अतन्द्रितः
अन्वहं तस्य वासाय श्वेतद्वीपः प्रकल्पितः ॥
61.m: For the one who unflaggingly remembers Nārāyaṇa continuously with devotion, / Śvetadvīpa is ordained for his daily dwelling.

61.s:
oṃkārādisamāyuktaṃ namaḥkārāntadīpitam
tannāma sarvatattvānāṃ mantra ity abhidhīyate //
61.d:
ओंकारादिसमायुक्तं नमःकारान्तदीपितम्
तन्नाम सर्वतत्त्वानां मन्त्र इत्य् अभिधीयते ॥
61.m: Joined with 'oṃ' at the beginning and illuminated by 'namaḥ' at the end, / that name of all principles is termed a mantra.

61.s:
anenaiva vidhānena gandhapuṣpaṃ nivedayet
ekaikasya prakurvīta yathoddiṣṭaṃ krameṇa tu //
61.d:
अनेनैव विधानेन गन्धपुष्पं निवेदयेत्
एकैकस्य प्रकुर्वीत यथोद्दिष्टं क्रमेण तु ॥
61.m: By this very rite one should offer fragrant paste and flowers; / one should perform [it] for each one in succession, as prescribed.

61.s:
mudrās tato nibadhnīyād yathoktakramacoditāḥ
japaṃ caiva prakurvīta mūlamantreṇa mantravit //
61.d:
मुद्रास् ततो निबध्नीयाद् यथोक्तक्रमचोदिताः
जपं चैव प्रकुर्वीत मूलमन्त्रेण मन्त्रवित् ॥
61.m: Then one should form the mudrās prescribed in the stated order; / and the knower of mantras should recite the primary mantra.

61.s:
aṣṭāviṃśatim aṣṭau vā śatam aṣṭottaraṃ tathā
kāmeṣu ca yathāproktaṃ yathāśakti samāhitaḥ //
61.d:
अष्टाविंशतिम् अष्टौ वा शतम् अष्टोत्तरं तथा
कामेषु च यथाप्रोक्तं यथाशक्ति समाहितः ॥
61.m: Twenty-eight, or eight, or a hundred and eight [times], / and for wishes as stated, concentrated according to one's capacity.

61.s:
padmaṃ śaṅkhaś ca śrīvatso gadā garuḍa eva ca
cakraṃ khaḍgaś ca śārṅgaṃ ca aṣṭau mudrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ //
61.d:
पद्मं शङ्खश् च श्रीवत्सो गदा गरुड एव च
चक्रं खड्गश् च शार्ङ्गं च अष्टौ मुद्राः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
61.m: Lotus, conch, Śrīvatsa, mace, and Garuḍa, / discus, sword, and Śārṅga: eight mudrās are proclaimed.

61.s:
visarjanamantraḥ
gaccha gaccha paraṃ sthānaṃ purāṇapuruṣottama
yatra brahmādayo devā vindanti paramaṃ padam //
61.d:
विसर्जनमन्त्रः
गच्छ गच्छ परं स्थानं पुराणपुरुषोत्तम
यत्र ब्रह्मादयो देवा विन्दन्ति परमं पदम् ॥
61.m: Mantra for dismissal: / Go, go to the supreme abode, ancient Puruṣottama, / where Brahmā and the other gods attain the supreme rank.

61.s:
arcanaṃ ye na jānanti harer mantrair yathoditam
te tatra mūlamantreṇa pūjayantv acyutaṃ sadā //
61.d:
अर्चनं ये न जानन्ति हरेर् मन्त्रैर् यथोदितम्
ते तत्र मूलमन्त्रेण पूजयन्त्व् अच्युतं सदा ॥
61.m: Those who do not know the worship of Hari with the mantras as described / should constantly worship Acyuta there with the primary mantra.

62.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ saṃpūjya vidhivad bhaktyā taṃ puruṣottamam
praṇamya śirasā paścāt sāgaraṃ ca prasādayet //
62.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं संपूज्य विधिवद् भक्त्या तं पुरुषोत्तमम्
प्रणम्य शिरसा पश्चात् सागरं च प्रसादयेत् ॥
62.m: Brahmā said: / Having thus worshipped that Puruṣottama according to rule with devotion, / having bowed with the head, one should afterwards propitiate the ocean:

62.s:
prāṇas tvaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ yoniś ca saritāṃ pate
tīrtharāja namas te 'stu trāhi mām acyutapriya //
62.d:
प्राणस् त्वं सर्वभूतानां योनिश् च सरितां पते
तीर्थराज नमस् ते ऽस्तु त्राहि माम् अच्युतप्रिय ॥
62.m: "You are the vital breath of all living beings and the source of streams, O lord of rivers! / O king of holy places, obeisance to you; protect me, O beloved of Acyuta!"

62.s:
snātvaivaṃ sāgare samyak tasmin kṣetravare dvijāḥ
tīre cābhyarcya vidhivan nārāyaṇam anāmayam //
62.d:
स्नात्वैवं सागरे सम्यक् तस्मिन् क्षेत्रवरे द्विजाः
तीरे चाभ्यर्च्य विधिवन् नारायणम् अनामयम् ॥
62.m: Having bathed thus properly in the ocean in that best of holy fields, O twice-born, / and having worshipped the flawless Nārāyaṇa on the shore according to rule,

62.s:
rāmaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ subhadrāṃ ca praṇipatya ca sāgaram
śatānām aśvamedhānāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ //
62.d:
रामं कृष्णं सुभद्रां च प्रणिपत्य च सागरम्
शतानाम् अश्वमेधानां फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः ॥
62.m: and having bowed down to Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Subhadrā, and the ocean, / a human being attains the fruit of a hundred horse sacrifices.

62.s:
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ sarvaduḥkhavivarjitaḥ
vṛndāraka iva śrīmān rūpayauvanagarvitaḥ //
62.d:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः सर्वदुःखविवर्जितः
वृन्दारक इव श्रीमान् रूपयौवनगर्वितः ॥
62.m: Freed from all sins, completely devoid of all sorrows, / like a god, glorious, proud of his beauty and youth,

62.s:
vimānenārkavarṇena divyagandharvanādinā
kulaikaviṃśam uddhṛtya viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati //
62.d:
विमानेनार्कवर्णेन दिव्यगन्धर्वनादिना
कुलैकविंशम् उद्धृत्य विष्णुलोकं स गच्छति ॥
62.m: by means of a flying chariot radiant as the sun, resounding with heavenly gandharvas, / having delivered twenty-one generations of his family, he goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

62.s:
bhuktvā tatra varān bhogān krīḍitvā cāpsaraiḥ saha
manvantaraśataṃ sāgraṃ jarāmṛtyuvivarjitaḥ //
62.d:
भुक्त्वा तत्र वरान् भोगान् क्रीडित्वा चाप्सरैः सह
मन्वन्तरशतं साग्रं जरामृत्युविवर्जितः ॥
62.m: Having enjoyed excellent delights there and sported with apsarases / for a full hundred Manvantaras, free from old age and death,

62.s:
puṇyakṣayād ihāyātaḥ kule sarvaguṇānvite
rūpavān subhagaḥ śrīmān satyavādī jitendriyaḥ //
62.d:
पुण्यक्षयाद् इहायातः कुले सर्वगुणान्विते
रूपवान् सुभगः श्रीमान् सत्यवादी जितेन्द्रियः ॥
62.m: having arrived back here through the exhaustion of merit, in a family endowed with all good qualities, / handsome, fortunate, glorious, truthful, with senses mastered,

62.s:
vedaśāstrārthavid vipro bhaved yajvā tu vaiṣṇavaḥ
yogaṃ ca vaiṣṇavaṃ prāpya tato mokṣam avāpnuyāt //
62.d:
वेदशास्त्रार्थविद् विप्रो भवेद् यज्वा तु वैष्णवः
योगं च वैष्णवं प्राप्य ततो मोक्षम् अवाप्नुयात् ॥
62.m: a twice-born knower of the meaning of the Vedas and treatises, a performer of sacrifices and a devotee of Viṣṇu, / and having attained the yoga of Viṣṇu, he then attains liberation.

62.s:
grahoparāge saṃkrāntyām ayane viṣuve tathā
yugādiṣu ṣaḍaśītyāṃ vyatīpāte dinakṣaye //
62.d:
ग्रहोपरागे संक्रान्त्याम् अयने विषुवे तथा
युगादिषु षडशीत्यां व्यतीपाते दिनक्षये ॥
62.m: During an eclipse of the planets, at a solstice, at an equinox, / at the beginnings of yugas, at a Saḍaśīti, at a Vyatīpāta, on a Dinakṣaya,

62.s:
āṣāḍhyāṃ caiva kārttikyāṃ māghyāṃ vānye śubhe tithau
ye tatra dānaṃ viprebhyaḥ prayacchanti sumedhasaḥ //
62.d:
आषाढ्यां चैव कार्त्तिक्यां माघ्यां वान्ये शुभे तिथौ
ये तत्र दानं विप्रेभ्यः प्रयच्छन्ति सुमेधसः ॥
62.m: on the full moon of Āṣāḍha, Kārttika, or Māgha, or on another auspicious lunar day, / the wise ones who offer gifts there to the twice-born

62.s:
phalaṃ sahasraguṇitam anyatīrthāl labhanti te
pitṝṇāṃ ye prayacchanti piṇḍaṃ tatra vidhānataḥ //
62.d:
फलं सहस्रगुणितम् अन्यतीर्थाल् लभन्ति ते
पितॄणां ये प्रयच्छन्ति पिण्डं तत्र विधानतः ॥
62.m: receive a reward a thousandfold greater than at any other holy place. / Those who offer rice balls there to the ancestors according to rule,

62.s:
akṣayāṃ pitaras teṣāṃ tṛptiṃ saṃprāpnuvanti vai
evaṃ snānaphalaṃ samyak sāgarasya mayoditam //
62.d:
अक्षयां पितरस् तेषां तृप्तिं संप्राप्नुवन्ति वै
एवं स्नानफलं सम्यक् सागरस्य मयोदितम् ॥
62.m: their ancestors indeed obtain inexhaustible satisfaction. / Thus has the complete fruit of bathing in the ocean been spoken by me,

62.s:
dānasya ca phalaṃ viprāḥ piṇḍadānasya caiva hi
dharmārthamokṣaphaladam āyuṣkīrtiyaśaskaram //
62.d:
दानस्य च फलं विप्राः पिण्डदानस्य चैव हि
धर्मार्थमोक्षफलदम् आयुष्कीर्तियशस्करम् ॥
62.m: as well as the fruit of giving, O twice-born, and of offering rice balls, / which grants the fruits of dharma, wealth, and liberation, and produces longevity, renown, and fame;

62.s:
bhuktimuktiphalaṃ nṝṇāṃ dhanyaṃ duḥsvapnanāśanam
sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradam //
62.d:
भुक्तिमुक्तिफलं नॄणां धन्यं दुःस्वप्ननाशनम्
सर्वपापहरं पुण्यं सर्वकामफलप्रदम् ॥
62.m: which yields worldly enjoyment and release for humans, is auspicious, destroys bad dreams, / removes all sins, is holy, and grants the fruits of all desires.

62.s:
nāstikāya na vaktavyaṃ purāṇaṃ ca dvijottamāḥ
tāvad garjanti tīrthāni māhātmyaiḥ svaiḥ pṛthak pṛthak //
62.d:
नास्तिकाय न वक्तव्यं पुराणं च द्विजोत्तमाः
तावद् गर्जन्ति तीर्थानि माहात्म्यैः स्वैः पृथक् पृथक् ॥
62.m: This Purāṇa must not be spoken to an unbeliever, O best of the twice-born! / Holy places roar with their separate greatnesses only so long

62.s:
yāvan na tīrtharājasya māhātmyaṃ varṇyate dvijāḥ
puṣkarādīni tīrthāni prayacchanti svakaṃ phalam //
62.d:
यावन् न तीर्थराजस्य माहात्म्यं वर्ण्यते द्विजाः
पुष्करादीनि तीर्थानि प्रयच्छन्ति स्वकं फलम् ॥
62.m: as the greatness of the king of holy places is not described, O twice-born! / Holy places such as Puṣkara grant their respective rewards,

62.s:
tīrtharājas tu sa punaḥ sarvatīrthaphalapradaḥ
bhūtale yāni tīrthāni saritaś ca sarāṃsi ca //
62.d:
तीर्थराजस् तु स पुनः सर्वतीर्थफलप्रदः
भूतले यानि तीर्थानि सरितश् च सरांसि च ॥
62.m: but the king of holy places, on the other hand, bestows the fruit of all holy places. / Whatever holy places, rivers, and lakes there are on the earth

62.s:
viśanti sāgare tāni tenāsau śreṣṭhatāṃ gataḥ
rājā samastatīrthānāṃ sāgaraḥ saritāṃ patiḥ //
62.d:
विशन्ति सागरे तानि तेनासौ श्रेष्ठतां गतः
राजा समस्ततीर्थानां सागरः सरितां पतिः ॥
62.m: enter the ocean; therefore it has attained preeminence. / The ocean, the lord of rivers, is the king of all holy places;

62.s:
tasmāt samastatīrthebhyaḥ śreṣṭho 'sau sarvakāmadaḥ
tamo nāśaṃ yathābhyeti bhāskare 'bhyudite dvijāḥ //
62.d:
तस्मात् समस्ततीर्थेभ्यः श्रेष्ठो ऽसौ सर्वकामदः
तमो नाशं यथाभ्येति भास्करे ऽभ्युदिते द्विजाः ॥
62.m: therefore it is superior to all holy places, the granter of all desires. / Just as darkness goes to destruction when the sun rises, O twice-born,

62.s:
snānena tīrtharājasya tathā pāpasya saṃkṣayaḥ
tīrtharājasamaṃ tīrthaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati //
62.d:
स्नानेन तीर्थराजस्य तथा पापस्य संक्षयः
तीर्थराजसमं तीर्थं न भूतं न भविष्यति ॥
62.m: so is sin destroyed by bathing in the king of holy places. / A holy place equal to the king of holy places never was, nor ever will be.

62.s:
adhiṣṭhānaṃ yadā yatra prabhor nārāyaṇasya vai
kaḥ śaknoti guṇān vaktuṃ tīrtharājasya bho dvijāḥ //
62.d:
अधिष्ठानं यदा यत्र प्रभोर् नारायणस्य वै
कः शक्नोति गुणान् वक्तुं तीर्थराजस्य भो द्विजाः ॥
62.m: When and where the residence of the lord Nārāyaṇa is truly there, / who is capable of describing the virtues of the king of holy places, O twice-born?

62.s:
koṭyo navanavatyas tu yatra tīrthāni santi vai
tasmāt snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca homaṃ japyaṃ surārcanam
yat kiṃcit kriyate tatra cākṣayaṃ kriyate dvijāḥ //
62.d:
कोट्यो नवनवत्यस् तु यत्र तीर्थानि सन्ति वै
तस्मात् स्नानं च दानं च होमं जप्यं सुरार्चनम्
यत् किंचित् क्रियते तत्र चाक्षयं क्रियते द्विजाः ॥
62.m: Where ninety-nine crores of holy places indeed exist, / therefore whatever bathing, giving, fire-offering, recitation, and worship of gods / is performed there, O twice-born, is made imperishable.

63.s:
brahmovāca
tato gacched dvijaśreṣṭhās tīrthaṃ yajñāṅgasaṃbhavam
indradyumnasaro nāma yatrāste pāvanaṃ śubham //
63.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततो गच्छेद् द्विजश्रेष्ठास् तीर्थं यज्ञाङ्गसंभवम्
इन्द्रद्युम्नसरो नाम यत्रास्ते पावनं शुभम् ॥
63.m: Brahmā said: / Then, O best of the twice-born, one should go to the holy place born of a part of the sacrifice, / named Indradyumna Lake, where the purifying, auspicious [water] resides.

63.s:
gatvā tatra śucir dhīmān ācamya manasā harim
dhyātvopasthāya ca jalam imaṃ mantram udīrayet //
63.d:
गत्वा तत्र शुचिर् धीमान् आचम्य मनसा हरिम्
ध्यात्वोपस्थाय च जलम् इमं मन्त्रम् उदीरयेत् ॥
63.m: Having gone there, pure and wise, having sipped water, having mentally / meditated upon Hari and approached the water, one should utter this mantra:

63.s:
aśvamedhāṅgasaṃbhūta tīrtha sarvāghanāśana
snānaṃ tvayi karomy adya pāpaṃ hara namo 'stu te //
63.d:
अश्वमेधाङ्गसंभूत तीर्थ सर्वाघनाशन
स्नानं त्वयि करोम्य् अद्य पापं हर नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
63.m: "O holy place born of an element of the horse sacrifice, destroyer of all sins, / I perform a bath in you today; take away sin, obeisance to you!"

63.s:
evam uccārya vidhivat snātvā devān ṛṣīn pitṝn
tilodakena cānyāṃś ca saṃtarpyācamya vāgyataḥ //
63.d:
एवम् उच्चार्य विधिवत् स्नात्वा देवान् ऋषीन् पितॄन्
तिलोदकेन चान्यांश् च संतर्प्याचम्य वाग्यतः ॥
63.m: Having spoken thus according to rule and bathed, having gratified the gods, sages, ancestors, / and others with sesame-water, and having sipped water, restrained in speech,

63.s:
dattvā pitṝṇāṃ piṇḍāṃś ca saṃpūjya puruṣottamam
daśāśvamedhikaṃ samyak phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ //
63.d:
दत्त्वा पितॄणां पिण्डांश् च संपूज्य पुरुषोत्तमम्
दशाश्वमेधिकं सम्यक् फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः ॥
63.m: Offering rice-balls to the ancestors and worshipping Puruṣottama, / a human being duly obtains the fruit of ten horse-sacrifices.

63.s:
saptāvarān sapta parān vaṃśān uddhṛtya devavat
kāmagena vimānena viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati //
63.d:
सप्तावरान् सप्त परान् वंशान् उद्धृत्य देववत्
कामगेन विमानेन विष्णुलोकं स गच्छति ॥
63.m: Having delivered seven previous and seven subsequent generations, / he goes like a god to the world of Viṣṇu in a wish-moving aerial chariot.

63.s:
bhuktvā tatra sukhān bhogān yāvac candrārkatārakam
cyutas tasmād ihāyāto mokṣaṃ ca labhate dhruvam //
63.d:
भुक्त्वा तत्र सुखान् भोगान् यावच् चन्द्रार्कतारकम्
च्युतस् तस्माद् इहायातो मोक्षं च लभते ध्रुवम् ॥
63.m: Having enjoyed pleasant pleasures there as long as the moon, sun, and stars endure, / falling from there and returning here, he surely attains liberation.

63.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā pañcatīrthīm ekādaśyām upoṣitaḥ
jyeṣṭhaśuklapañcadaśyāṃ yaḥ paśyet puruṣottamam //
63.d:
एवं कृत्वा पञ्चतीर्थीम् एकादश्याम् उपोषितः
ज्येष्ठशुक्लपञ्चदश्यां यः पश्येत् पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
63.m: Having thus performed the pilgrimage to the five sacred sites, fasting on the eleventh day, / whoever beholds Puruṣottama on the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight of Jyeṣṭha,

63.s:
sa pūrvoktaṃ phalaṃ prāpya krīḍitvā vācyutālaye
prayāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yasmān nāvartate punaḥ //
63.d:
स पूर्वोक्तं फलं प्राप्य क्रीडित्वा वाच्युतालये
प्रयाति परमं स्थानं यस्मान् नावर्तते पुनः ॥
63.m: attaining that aforementioned fruit and sporting in the abode of Acyuta, / goes to the supreme state from which he does not return again.

63.s:
munaya ūcuḥ
māsān anyān parityajya māghādīn prapitāmaha
praśaṃsasi kathaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ brūhi tatkāraṇaṃ prabho //
63.d:
मुनय ऊचुः
मासान् अन्यान् परित्यज्य माघादीन् प्रपितामह
प्रशंससि कथं ज्येष्ठं ब्रूहि तत्कारणं प्रभो ॥
63.m: The sages said: / Leaving aside other months, such as Māgha and the rest, O great-grandfather, / why do you praise Jyeṣṭha? Tell us the reason for that, O Lord!

63.s:
brahmovāca
śṛṇudhvaṃ muniśārdūlāḥ pravakṣyāmi samāsataḥ
jyeṣṭhaṃ māsaṃ yathā tebhyaḥ praśaṃsāmi punaḥ punaḥ //
63.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
शृणुध्वं मुनिशार्दूलाः प्रवक्ष्यामि समासतः
ज्येष्ठं मासं यथा तेभ्यः प्रशंसामि पुनः पुनः ॥
63.m: Brahmā said: / Listen, O tigers among sages; I shall explain in brief / why I praise the month of Jyeṣṭha above them again and again.

63.s:
pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni saritaś ca sarāṃsi ca
puṣkariṇyas taḍāgāni vāpyaḥ kūpās tathā hradāḥ //
63.d:
पृथिव्यां यानि तीर्थानि सरितश् च सरांसि च
पुष्करिण्यस् तडागानि वाप्यः कूपास् तथा ह्रदाः ॥
63.m: Whatever sacred places, rivers, and lakes are on the earth, / lotus ponds, reservoirs, stepwells, wells, and pools,

63.s:
nānānadyaḥ samudrāś ca saptāhaṃ puruṣottame
jyeṣṭhaśukladaśamyādi pratyakṣaṃ yānti sarvadā //
63.d:
नानानद्यः समुद्राश् च सप्ताहं पुरुषोत्तमे
ज्येष्ठशुक्लदशम्यादि प्रत्यक्षं यान्ति सर्वदा ॥
63.m: various streams and oceans, for seven days in Puruṣottama, / from the tenth day of the bright fortnight of Jyeṣṭha onwards, are always visibly present.

63.s:
snānadānādikaṃ tasmād devatāprekṣaṇaṃ dvijāḥ
yat kiṃcit kriyate tatra tasmin kāle 'kṣayaṃ bhavet //
63.d:
स्नानदानादिकं तस्माद् देवताप्रेक्षणं द्विजाः
यत् किंचित् क्रियते तत्र तस्मिन् काले ऽक्षयं भवेत् ॥
63.m: Therefore, O twice-born, bathing, giving gifts, and the like, and the beholding of the deity— / whatever little is done there at that time becomes imperishable.

63.s:
śuklapakṣasya daśamī jyeṣṭhe māsi dvijottamāḥ
harate daśa pāpāni tasmād daśaharā smṛtā //
63.d:
शुक्लपक्षस्य दशमी ज्येष्ठे मासि द्विजोत्तमाः
हरते दश पापानि तस्माद् दशहरा स्मृता ॥
63.m: The tenth day of the bright fortnight in the month of Jyeṣṭha, O best of the twice-born, / removes ten sins; therefore it is traditionally called Daśaharā.

63.s:
yas tasyāṃ halinaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ paśyed bhadrāṃ susaṃyataḥ
sarvapāpavinirmukto viṣṇulokaṃ vrajen naraḥ //
63.d:
यस् तस्यां हलिनं कृष्णं पश्येद् भद्रां सुसंयतः
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो विष्णुलोकं व्रजेन् नरः ॥
63.m: A man who, well-restrained, beholds on it the plow-holder, Kṛṣṇa, and Bhadrā, / freed from all sins, goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

63.s:
uttare dakṣiṇe viprās tv ayane puruṣottamam
dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ subhadrāṃ ca viṣṇulokaṃ vrajen naraḥ //
63.d:
उत्तरे दक्षिणे विप्रास् त्व् अयने पुरुषोत्तमम्
दृष्ट्वा रामं सुभद्रां च विष्णुलोकं व्रजेन् नरः ॥
63.m: At the northern and the southern solstices, O brahmins, / a man who beholds Puruṣottama, Rāma, and Subhadrā goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

63.s:
naro dolāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā govindaṃ puruṣottamam
phālgunyāṃ prayato bhūtvā govindasya puraṃ vrajet //
63.d:
नरो दोलागतं दृष्ट्वा गोविन्दं पुरुषोत्तमम्
फाल्गुन्यां प्रयतो भूत्वा गोविन्दस्य पुरं व्रजेत् ॥
63.m: A man who, having become restrained, beholds Govinda, Puruṣottama, seated on a swing / on the full-moon day of Phālguna, goes to the city of Govinda.

63.s:
viṣuvaddivase prāpte pañcatīrthīṃ vidhānataḥ
kṛtvā saṃkarṣaṇaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhadrāṃ ca bho dvijāḥ //
63.d:
विषुवद्दिवसे प्राप्ते पञ्चतीर्थीं विधानतः
कृत्वा संकर्षणं कृष्णं दृष्ट्वा भद्रां च भो द्विजाः ॥
63.m: When the day of the equinox arrives, having performed the pilgrimage to the five sacred sites according to rule / and beheld Saṃkarṣaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, and Bhadrā, O twice-born,

63.s:
naraḥ samastayajñānāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti durlabham
vimuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyo viṣṇulokaṃ ca gacchati //
63.d:
नरः समस्तयज्ञानां फलं प्राप्नोति दुर्लभम्
विमुक्तः सर्वपापेभ्यो विष्णुलोकं च गच्छति ॥
63.m: a man obtains the hard-to-attain fruit of all sacrifices; / freed from all sins, he goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

63.s:
yaḥ paśyati tṛtīyāyāṃ kṛṣṇaṃ candanarūṣitam
vaiśākhasyāsite pakṣe sa yāty acyutamandiram //
63.d:
यः पश्यति तृतीयायां कृष्णं चन्दनरूषितम्
वैशाखस्यासिते पक्षे स यात्य् अच्युतमन्दिरम् ॥
63.m: He who beholds Kṛṣṇa smeared with sandalwood on the third day / in the dark fortnight of Vaiśākha, goes to the abode of Acyuta.

63.s:
jyaiṣṭhyāṃ jyeṣṭharkṣayuktāyāṃ yaḥ paśyet puruṣottamam
kulaikaviṃśam uddhṛtya viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati //
63.d:
ज्यैष्ठ्यां ज्येष्ठर्क्षयुक्तायां यः पश्येत् पुरुषोत्तमम्
कुलैकविंशम् उद्धृत्य विष्णुलोकं स गच्छति ॥
63.m: He who beholds Puruṣottama on the full moon of Jyeṣṭha joined with the lunar mansion Jyeṣṭhā, / having delivered twenty-one generations of his family, goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

64.s:
brahmovāca
yadā bhaven mahājyaiṣṭhī rāśinakṣatrayogataḥ
prayatnena tadā martyair gantavyaṃ puruṣottamam //
64.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
यदा भवेन् महाज्यैष्ठी राशिनक्षत्रयोगतः
प्रयत्नेन तदा मर्त्यैर् गन्तव्यं पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
64.m: Brahmā said: / When there occurs the Mahājyaiṣṭhī due to the conjunction of the zodiac sign and lunar mansion, / Puruṣottama should then be visited with great effort by mortals.

64.s:
kṛṣṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahājyaiṣṭhyāṃ rāmaṃ bhadrāṃ ca bho dvijāḥ
naro dvādaśayātrāyāḥ phalaṃ prāpnoti cādhikam //
64.d:
कृष्णं दृष्ट्वा महाज्यैष्ठ्यां रामं भद्रां च भो द्विजाः
नरो द्वादशयात्रायाः फलं प्राप्नोति चाधिकम् ॥
64.m: Having beheld Kṛṣṇa, Rāma, and Bhadrā on the Mahājyaiṣṭhī, O twice-born, / a man obtains a fruit greater than [that of] the twelve festivals.

64.s:
prayāge ca kurukṣetre naimiṣe puṣkare gaye
gaṅgādvāre kuśāvarte gaṅgāsāgarasaṃgame //
64.d:
प्रयागे च कुरुक्षेत्रे नैमिषे पुष्करे गये
गङ्गाद्वारे कुशावर्ते गङ्गासागरसंगमे ॥
64.m: At Prayāga, Kurukṣetra, Naimiṣa, Puṣkara, Gayā, / Gaṅgādvāra, Kuśāvarta, the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean;

64.s:
kokāmukhe śūkare ca mathurāyāṃ marusthale
śālagrāme vāyutīrthe mandare sindhusāgare //
64.d:
कोकामुखे शूकरे च मथुरायां मरुस्थले
शालग्रामे वायुतीर्थे मन्दरे सिन्धुसागरे ॥
64.m: at Kokāmukha, Śūkara, Mathurā, Marusthala, / Śālagrāma, Vāyutīrtha, Mandara, the Sindhu ocean;

64.s:
piṇḍārake citrakūṭe prabhāse kanakhale dvijāḥ
śaṅkhoddhāre dvārakāyāṃ tathā badarikāśrame //
64.d:
पिण्डारके चित्रकूटे प्रभासे कनखले द्विजाः
शङ्खोद्धारे द्वारकायां तथा बदरिकाश्रमे ॥
64.m: at Piṇḍāraka, Citrakūṭa, Prabhāsa, Kanakhala, O twice-born; / at Śaṅkhoddhāra, Dvārakā, and likewise at Badarikāśrama;

64.s:
lohakuṇḍe cāśvatīrthe sarvapāpapramocane
kāmālaye koṭitīrthe tathā cāmarakaṇṭake //
64.d:
लोहकुण्डे चाश्वतीर्थे सर्वपापप्रमोचने
कामालये कोटितीर्थे तथा चामरकण्टके ॥
64.m: at Lohakuṇḍa, Aśvatīrtha, Sarvapāpapramocana, / Kāmālaya, Koṭitīrtha, and likewise at Amarakaṇṭaka;

64.s:
lohārgale jambumārge somatīrthe pṛthūdake
utpalāvartake caiva pṛthutuṅge sukubjake //
64.d:
लोहार्गले जम्बुमार्गे सोमतीर्थे पृथूदके
उत्पलावर्तके चैव पृथुतुङ्गे सुकुब्जके ॥
64.m: at Lohārgala, Jambumārga, Somatīrtha, Pṛthūdaka, / Utpalāvartaka, Pṛthutuṅga, Sukubjaka;

64.s:
ekāmrake ca kedāre kāśyāṃ ca viraje dvijāḥ
kālañjare ca gokarṇe śrīśaile gandhamādane //
64.d:
एकाम्रके च केदारे काश्यां च विरजे द्विजाः
कालञ्जरे च गोकर्णे श्रीशैले गन्धमादने ॥
64.m: at Ekāmraka, Kedāra, Kāśī, and Viraja, O twice-born; / at Kālañjara, Gokarṇa, Śrīśaila, Gandhamādana;

64.s:
mahendre malaye vindhye pāriyātre himālaye
sahye ca śuktimante ca gomante cārbude tathā //
64.d:
महेन्द्रे मलये विन्ध्ये पारियात्रे हिमालये
सह्ये च शुक्तिमन्ते च गोमन्ते चार्बुदे तथा ॥
64.m: on the Mahendra, Malaya, Vindhya, Pāriyātra, and Himālaya [mountains]; / on the Sahya, Śuktimat, Gomanta, and Arbuda;

64.s:
gaṅgāyāṃ sarvatīrtheṣu yāmuneṣu ca bho dvijāḥ
sārasvateṣu gomatyāṃ brahmaputreṣu saptasu //
64.d:
गङ्गायां सर्वतीर्थेषु यामुनेषु च भो द्विजाः
सारस्वतेषु गोमत्यां ब्रह्मपुत्रेषु सप्तसु ॥
64.m: at the Gaṅgā, at all sacred places at the Yamunā, O twice-born, / at those along the Sarasvatī, at the Gomatī, and at the seven Brahmaputras;

64.s:
godāvarī bhīmarathī tuṅgabhadrā ca narmadā
tāpī payouṣṇī kāverī śiprā carmaṇvatī dvijāḥ //
64.d:
गोदावरी भीमरथी तुङ्गभद्रा च नर्मदा
तापी पयोउष्णी कावेरी शिप्रा चर्मण्वती द्विजाः ॥
64.m: at the Godāvarī, Bhīmarathī, Tuṅgabhadrā, and Narmadā; / Tāpī, Payoṣṇī, Kāverī, Śiprā, and Carmaṇvatī, O twice-born;

64.s:
vitastā candrabhāgā ca śatadrur bāhudā tathā
ṛṣikulyā kumārī ca vipāśā ca dṛṣadvatī //
64.d:
वितस्ता चन्द्रभागा च शतद्रुर् बाहुदा तथा
ऋषिकुल्या कुमारी च विपाशा च दृषद्वती ॥
64.m: at the Vitastā, Candrabhāgā, Śatadru, and Bāhudā; / Ṛṣikulyā, Kumārī, Vipāśā, and Dṛṣadvatī;

64.s:
śarayūr nākagaṅgā ca gaṇḍakī ca mahānadī
kauśikī karatoyā ca trisrotā madhuvāhinī //
64.d:
शरयूर् नाकगङ्गा च गण्डकी च महानदी
कौशिकी करतोया च त्रिस्रोता मधुवाहिनी ॥
64.m: at the Śarayū, Nākagaṅgā, Gaṇḍakī, and Mahānadī; / Kauśikī, Karatoyā, Trisrotas, and Madhuvāhinī;

64.s:
mahānadī vaitaraṇī yāś cānyā nānukīrtitāḥ
athavā kiṃ bahūktena bhāṣitena dvijottamāḥ //
64.d:
महानदी वैतरणी याश् चान्या नानुकीर्तिताः
अथवा किं बहूक्तेन भाषितेन द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
64.m: at the Mahānadī, Vaitaraṇī, and the others not mentioned— / or what need is there to speak at great length, O best of the twice-born?

64.s:
pṛthivyāṃ sarvatīrtheṣu sarveṣv āyataneṣu ca
sāgareṣu ca śaileṣu nadīṣu ca saraḥsu ca //
64.d:
पृथिव्यां सर्वतीर्थेषु सर्वेष्व् आयतनेषु च
सागरेषु च शैलेषु नदीषु च सरःसु च ॥
64.m: At all the sacred sites on earth, and in all temples, / in oceans, on mountains, in rivers, and in lakes,

64.s:
yat phalaṃ snānadānena rāhugraste divākare
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mahājyaiṣṭhyāṃ labhen naraḥ //
64.d:
यत् फलं स्नानदानेन राहुग्रस्ते दिवाकरे
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य महाज्यैष्ठ्यां लभेन् नरः ॥
64.m: whatever fruit [is gained] by bathing and giving gifts when the sun is seized by Rāhu, / a man obtains that fruit upon beholding Kṛṣṇa on the Mahājyaiṣṭhī.

64.s:
tasmāt sarvaprayatnena gantavyaṃ puruṣottame
mahājyaiṣṭhyāṃ muniśreṣṭhā sarvakāmaphalepsubhiḥ //
64.d:
तस्मात् सर्वप्रयत्नेन गन्तव्यं पुरुषोत्तमे
महाज्यैष्ठ्यां मुनिश्रेष्ठा सर्वकामफलेप्सुभिः ॥
64.m: Therefore, by every effort, Puruṣottama should be visited / on the Mahājyaiṣṭhī, O best of sages, by those desiring the fruit of all wishes.

64.s:
dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ mahājyeṣṭhaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ subhadrayā saha
viṣṇulokaṃ naro yāti samuddhṛtya samaṃ kulam //
64.d:
दृष्ट्वा रामं महाज्येष्ठं कृष्णं सुभद्रया सह
विष्णुलोकं नरो याति समुद्धृत्य समं कुलम् ॥
64.m: Having beheld Rāma, the eldest, [and] Kṛṣṇa together with Subhadrā, / a man goes to the world of Viṣṇu, having thoroughly delivered his entire family.

64.s:
bhuktvā tatra varān bhogān yāvad ābhūtasaṃplavam
puṇyakṣayād ihāgatya caturvedī dvijo bhavet //
64.d:
भुक्त्वा तत्र वरान् भोगान् यावद् आभूतसंप्लवम्
पुण्यक्षयाद् इहागत्य चतुर्वेदी द्विजो भवेत् ॥
64.m: Having enjoyed excellent pleasures there until the cosmic dissolution, / coming here upon the exhaustion of his merit, he becomes a twice-born master of the four Vedas.

64.s:
svadharmanirataḥ śāntaḥ kṛṣṇabhakto jitendriyaḥ
vaiṣṇavaṃ yogam āsthāya tato mokṣam avāpnuyāt //
64.d:
स्वधर्मनिरतः शान्तः कृष्णभक्तो जितेन्द्रियः
वैष्णवं योगम् आस्थाय ततो मोक्षम् अवाप्नुयात् ॥
64.m: Devoted to his own dharma, tranquil, devoted to Kṛṣṇa, with senses conquered, / resorting to Vaiṣṇava yoga, he then attains liberation.

65.s:
munaya ūcuḥ
kasmin kāle bhavet snānaṃ kṛṣṇasya kamalodbhava
vidhinā kena tad brūhi tato vidhividāṃ vara //
65.d:
मुनय ऊचुः
कस्मिन् काले भवेत् स्नानं कृष्णस्य कमलोद्भव
विधिना केन तद् ब्रूहि ततो विधिविदां वर ॥
65.m: The sages said: / At what time does the bathing of Kṛṣṇa take place, O lotus-born one, / and by what rite? Tell us that then, O best among those who know ritual!

65.s:
brahmovāca
śṛṇudhvaṃ munayaḥ snānaṃ kṛṣṇasya vadato mama
rāmasya ca subhadrāyāḥ puṇyaṃ sarvāghanāśanam //
65.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
शृणुध्वं मुनयः स्नानं कृष्णस्य वदतो मम
रामस्य च सुभद्रायाः पुण्यं सर्वाघनाशनम् ॥
65.m: Brahmā said: / Listen, O sages, as I declare the bathing of Kṛṣṇa, / of Rāma, and of Subhadrā—auspicious and destroying all sin.

65.s:
māsi jyeṣṭhe ca saṃprāpte nakṣatre candradaivate
paurṇamāsyāṃ tadā snānaṃ sarvakālaṃ harer dvijāḥ //
65.d:
मासि ज्येष्ठे च संप्राप्ते नक्षत्रे चन्द्रदैवते
पौर्णमास्यां तदा स्नानं सर्वकालं हरेर् द्विजाः ॥
65.m: When the month of Jyeṣṭha arrives, under the lunar mansion whose deity is the Moon, / on the full-moon day, then is the bathing of Hari for all time, O twice-born.

65.s:
sarvatīrthamayaḥ kūpas tatrāste nirmalaḥ śuciḥ
tadā bhogavatī tatra pratyakṣā bhavati dvijāḥ //
65.d:
सर्वतीर्थमयः कूपस् तत्रास्ते निर्मलः शुचिः
तदा भोगवती तत्र प्रत्यक्षा भवति द्विजाः ॥
65.m: There is a pure, clean well there, containing all sacred waters; / then the Bhogavatī becomes visibly manifest there, O twice-born.

65.s:
tasmāj jyaiṣṭhyāṃ samuddhṛtya haimāḍhyaiḥ kalaśair jalam
kṛṣṇarāmābhiṣekārthaṃ subhadrāyāś ca bho dvijāḥ //
65.d:
तस्माज् ज्यैष्ठ्यां समुद्धृत्य हैमाढ्यैः कलशैर् जलम्
कृष्णरामाभिषेकार्थं सुभद्रायाश् च भो द्विजाः ॥
65.m: Drawing water from it on the full moon of Jyeṣṭha with pitchers adorned with gold / for the consecration of Kṛṣṇa and Rāma, and of Subhadrā, O twice-born,

65.s:
kṛtvā suśobhanaṃ mañcaṃ patākābhir alaṃkṛtam
sudṛḍhaṃ sukhasaṃcāraṃ vastraiḥ puṣpair alaṃkṛtam //
65.d:
कृत्वा सुशोभनं मञ्चं पताकाभिर् अलंकृतम्
सुदृढं सुखसंचारं वस्त्रैः पुष्पैर् अलंकृतम् ॥
65.m: having constructed a very splendid platform adorned with flags, / very firm, allowing easy movement, embellished with garments and flowers,

65.s:
vistīrṇaṃ dhūpitaṃ dhūpaiḥ snānārthaṃ rāmakṛṣṇayoḥ
sitavastraparicchannaṃ muktāhārāvalambitam //
65.d:
विस्तीर्णं धूपितं धूपैः स्नानार्थं रामकृष्णयोः
सितवस्त्रपरिच्छन्नं मुक्ताहारावलम्बितम् ॥
65.m: spacious, perfumed with incense, for the bathing of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, / covered with white cloth and hung with pearl necklaces—

65.s:
tatra nānāvidhair vādyaiḥ kṛṣṇaṃ nīlāmbaraṃ dvijāḥ
madhye subhadrāṃ cāsthāpya jayamaṅgalanisvanaiḥ //
65.d:
तत्र नानाविधैर् वाद्यैः कृष्णं नीलाम्बरं द्विजाः
मध्ये सुभद्रां चास्थाप्य जयमङ्गलनिस्वनैः ॥
65.m: placing Kṛṣṇa, [Rāma] clad in blue garments, and Subhadrā in the middle there / with various musical instruments and shouts of victory and blessing, O twice-born,

65.s:
brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriyair vaiśyaiḥ śūdraiś cānyaiś ca jātibhiḥ
anekaśatasāhasrair vṛtaṃ strīpuruṣair dvijāḥ //
65.d:
ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर् वैश्यैः शूद्रैश् चान्यैश् च जातिभिः
अनेकशतसाहस्रैर् वृतं स्त्रीपुरुषैर् द्विजाः ॥
65.m: surrounded by brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, and other classes, / by many hundreds of thousands of men and women, O twice-born—

65.s:
gṛhasthāḥ snātakāś caiva yatayo brahmacāriṇaḥ
snāpayanti tadā kṛṣṇaṃ mañcasthaṃ sahalāyudham //
65.d:
गृहस्थाः स्नातकाश् चैव यतयो ब्रह्मचारिणः
स्नापयन्ति तदा कृष्णं मञ्चस्थं सहलायुधम् ॥
65.m:
Householders, snātakas, ascetics, and brahmacārins
then bathe Kṛṣṇa, standing upon the dais together with Halāyudha.

65.s:
tathā samastatīrthāni pūrvoktāni dvijottamāḥ
svodakaiḥ puṣpamiśraiś ca snāpayanti pṛthak pṛthak //
65.d:
तथा समस्ततीर्थानि पूर्वोक्तानि द्विजोत्तमाः
स्वोदकैः पुष्पमिश्रैश् च स्नापयन्ति पृथक् पृथक् ॥
65.m:
Likewise, O best of twice-borns, all the previously mentioned sacred pilgrimage sites
bathe [them] individually with their own waters mixed with flowers.

65.s:
paścāt paṭahaśaṅkhādyair bherīmurajanisvanaiḥ
kāhalais tālaśabdaiś ca mṛdaṅgair jharjharais tathā //
65.d:
पश्चात् पटहशङ्खाद्यैर् भेरीमुरजनिस्वनैः
काहलैस् तालशब्दैश् च मृदङ्गैर् झर्झरैस् तथा ॥
65.m:
Afterwards, with kettle-drums, conches, and other instruments, with the sounds of bherī and muraja drums,
with trumpets and the sounds of cymbals, with mṛdaṅgas and jharjharas,

65.s:
anyaiś ca vividhair vādyair ghaṇṭāsvanavibhūṣitaiḥ
strīṇāṃ maṅgalaśabdaiś ca stutiśabdair manoharaiḥ //
65.d:
अन्यैश् च विविधैर् वाद्यैर् घण्टास्वनविभूषितैः
स्त्रीणां मङ्गलशब्दैश् च स्तुतिशब्दैर् मनोहरैः ॥
65.m:
and with various other musical instruments adorned by the sound of bells,
with the auspicious sounds of women and enchanting sounds of praise,

65.s:
jayaśabdais tathā stotrair vīṇāveṇunināditaiḥ
śrūyate sumahāñ śabdaḥ sāgarasyeva garjataḥ //
65.d:
जयशब्दैस् तथा स्तोत्रैर् वीणावेणुनिनादितैः
श्रूयते सुमहाञ् शब्दः सागरस्येव गर्जतः ॥
65.m:
with shouts of victory, hymns, and the melodious sounds of lute and flute,
a tremendous roar is heard, like that of the roaring ocean.

65.s:
munīnāṃ vedaśabdena mantraśabdais tathāparaiḥ
nānāstotraravaiḥ puṇyaiḥ sāmaśabdopabṛṃhitaiḥ //
65.d:
मुनीनां वेदशब्देन मन्त्रशब्दैस् तथापरैः
नानास्तोत्ररवैः पुण्यैः सामशब्दोपबृंहितैः ॥
65.m:
Through the sound of the Vedas of the sages, and through other mantra-sounds,
through the holy sounds of various hymns, magnified by the sounds of the Sāman chants,

65.s:
yatibhiḥ snātakaiś caiva gṛhasthair brahmacāribhiḥ
snānakāle suraśreṣṭha stuvanti parayā mudā //
65.d:
यतिभिः स्नातकैश् चैव गृहस्थैर् ब्रह्मचारिभिः
स्नानकाले सुरश्रेष्ठ स्तुवन्ति परया मुदा ॥
65.m:
by ascetics, snātakas, householders, and brahmacārins,
at the time of the bath, O best among the gods, they praise [him] with supreme joy.

65.s:
śyāmair veśyājanaiś caiva kucabhārāvanāmibhiḥ
pītaraktāmbarābhiś ca mālyadāmāvanāmibhiḥ //
65.d:
श्यामैर् वेश्याजनैश् चैव कुचभारावनामिभिः
पीतरक्ताम्बराभिश् च माल्यदामावनामिभिः ॥
65.m:
By dark-complexioned courtesans bending under the weight of their breasts,
wearing yellow and red garments, bending under strings of flower-garlands,

65.s:
saratnakuṇḍalair divyaiḥ suvarṇastabakānvitaiḥ
cāmarai ratnadaṇḍaiś ca vījyete rāmakeśavau //
65.d:
सरत्नकुण्डलैर् दिव्यैः सुवर्णस्तबकान्वितैः
चामरै रत्नदण्डैश् च वीज्येते रामकेशवौ ॥
65.m:
with divine jewel-studded earrings and adorned with golden clusters,
with chowries having jeweled handles, Rāma and Keśava are fanned.

65.s:
yakṣavidyādharaiḥ siddhaiḥ kiṃnaraiś cāpsarogaṇaiḥ
parivāryāmbaragatair devagandharvacāraṇaiḥ //
65.d:
यक्षविद्याधरैः सिद्धैः किंनरैश् चाप्सरोगणैः
परिवार्याम्बरगतैर् देवगन्धर्वचारणैः ॥
65.m:
By Yakṣas, Vidyādharas, Siddhas, Kiṃnaras, and troops of Apsarases,
standing in the sky and surrounding [them], by celestial Gandharvas and Cāraṇas,

65.s:
ādityā vasavo rudrāḥ sādhyā viśve marudgaṇāḥ
lokapālās tathā cānye stuvanti puruṣottamam //
65.d:
आदित्या वसवो रुद्राः साध्या विश्वे मरुद्गणाः
लोकपालास् तथा चान्ये स्तुवन्ति पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
65.m:
the Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Sādhyas, Viśvedevas, Marut-troops,
and the world-guardians and others praise Puruṣottama:

65.s:
namas te devadeveśa purāṇa puruṣottama
sargasthityantakṛd deva lokanātha jagatpate //
65.d:
नमस् ते देवदेवेश पुराण पुरुषोत्तम
सर्गस्थित्यन्तकृद् देव लोकनाथ जगत्पते ॥
65.m:
"Homage to you, O Lord of the gods of gods, ancient one, O Puruṣottama,
O God, creator of primary creation, preservation, and dissolution, protector of the world, Lord of the universe!

65.s:
trailokyadhāriṇaṃ devaṃ brahmaṇyaṃ mokṣakāraṇam
taṃ namasyāmahe bhaktyā sarvakāmaphalapradam //
65.d:
त्रैलोक्यधारिणं देवं ब्रह्मण्यं मोक्षकारणम्
तं नमस्यामहे भक्त्या सर्वकामफलप्रदम् ॥
65.m:
The god who upholds the three worlds, benevolent to brāhmaṇas, the cause of liberation,
to him we bow in devotion, the granter of the fruit of all desires!"

65.s:
stutvaivaṃ vibudhāḥ kṛṣṇaṃ rāmaṃ caiva mahābalam
subhadrāṃ ca muniśreṣṭhās tadākāśe vyavasthitāḥ //
65.d:
स्तुत्वैवं विबुधाः कृष्णं रामं चैव महाबलम्
सुभद्रां च मुनिश्रेष्ठास् तदाकाशे व्यवस्थिताः ॥
65.m:
Having thus praised Kṛṣṇa, the mighty Rāma,
and Subhadrā, the gods, O best of sages, stood there in the sky.

65.s:
gāyanti devagandharvā nṛtyanty apsarasas tathā
devatūryāṇy avādyanta vātā vānti suśītalāḥ //
65.d:
गायन्ति देवगन्धर्वा नृत्यन्त्य् अप्सरसस् तथा
देवतूर्याण्य् अवाद्यन्त वाता वान्ति सुशीतलाः ॥
65.m:
The celestial Gandharvas sing, and the Apsarases dance;
celestial musical instruments were sounded, and very cool breezes blow.

65.s:
puṣpamiśraṃ tadā meghā varṣanty ākāśagocarāḥ
jayaśabdaṃ ca kurvanti munayaḥ siddhacāraṇāḥ //
65.d:
पुष्पमिश्रं तदा मेघा वर्षन्त्य् आकाशगोचराः
जयशब्दं च कुर्वन्ति मुनयः सिद्धचारणाः ॥
65.m:
Then the clouds moving in the sky shower [rain] mixed with flowers,
and the sages, Siddhas, and Cāraṇas utter cries of victory.

65.s:
śakrādyā vibudhāḥ sarva ṛṣayaḥ pitaras tathā
prajānāṃ patayo nāgā ye cānye svargavāsinaḥ //
65.d:
शक्राद्या विबुधाः सर्व ऋषयः पितरस् तथा
प्रजानां पतयो नागा ये चान्ये स्वर्गवासिनः ॥
65.m:
All the gods led by Śakra, the ṛṣis, the ancestors,
the lords of creatures, the serpents, and whatever other dwellers of heaven there are—

65.s:
tato maṅgalasaṃbhārair vidhimantrapuraskṛtam
ābhiṣecanikaṃ dravyaṃ gṛhītvā devatāgaṇāḥ //
65.d:
ततो मङ्गलसंभारैर् विधिमन्त्रपुरस्कृतम्
आभिषेचनिकं द्रव्यं गृहीत्वा देवतागणाः ॥
65.m:
then the hosts of deities, taking the ingredients for consecration
accompanied by auspicious preparations and preceded by Vedic rites and mantras,

65.s:
indro viṣṇur mahāvīryaḥ sūryācandramasau tathā
dhātā caiva vidhātā ca tathā caivānilānalau //
65.d:
इन्द्रो विष्णुर् महावीर्यः सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ तथा
धाता चैव विधाता च तथा चैवानिलानलौ ॥
65.m:
Indra, Viṣṇu of great prowess, and the sun and moon,
Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ, and also wind and fire,

65.s:
pūṣā bhago 'ryamā tvaṣṭā aṃśunaiva vivasvatā
patnībhyāṃ sahito dhīmān mitreṇa varuṇena ca //
65.d:
पूषा भगो ऽर्यमा त्वष्टा अंशुनैव विवस्वता
पत्नीभ्यां सहितो धीमान् मित्रेण वरुणेन च ॥
65.m:
Pūṣan, Bhaga, Aryaman, Tvaṣṭṛ, along with Aṃśu and Vivasvat,
accompanied by his two wives, the wise one, along with Mitra and Varuṇa,

65.s:
rudrair vasubhir ādityair aśvibhyāṃ ca vṛtaḥ prabhuḥ
viśvair devair marudbhiś ca sādhyaiś ca pitṛbhiḥ saha //
65.d:
रुद्रैर् वसुभिर् आदित्यैर् अश्विभ्यां च वृतः प्रभुः
विश्वैर् देवैर् मरुद्भिश् च साध्यैश् च पितृभिः सह ॥
65.m:
the Lord surrounded by the Rudras, Vasus, Ādityas, and the two Aśvins,
along with the Viśvedevas, Maruts, Sādhyas, and Pitṛs,

65.s:
gandharvair apsarobhiś ca yakṣarākṣasapannagaiḥ
devarṣibhir asaṃkhyeyais tathā brahmarṣibhir varaiḥ //
65.d:
गन्धर्वैर् अप्सरोभिश् च यक्षराक्षसपन्नगैः
देवर्षिभिर् असंख्येयैस् तथा ब्रह्मर्षिभिर् वरैः ॥
65.m:
with Gandharvas, Apsarases, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Pannagas,
with countless divine sages, and also with excellent brahmarṣis,

65.s:
vaikhānasair vālakhilyair vāyvāhārair marīcipaiḥ
bhṛgubhiś cāṅgirobhiś ca sarvavidyāsuniṣṭhitaiḥ //
65.d:
वैखानसैर् वालखिल्यैर् वाय्वाहारैर् मरीचिपैः
भृगुभिश् चाङ्गिरोभिश् च सर्वविद्यासुनिष्ठितैः ॥
65.m:
with the Vaikhānasa and Vālakhilya hermits, those feeding on air, those drinking rays of light,
with the Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases, completely established in all knowledge,

65.s:
sarvavidyādharaiḥ puṇyair yogasiddhibhir āvṛtaḥ
pitāmahaḥ pulastyaś ca pulahaś ca mahātapāḥ //
65.d:
सर्वविद्याधरैः पुण्यैर् योगसिद्धिभिर् आवृतः
पितामहः पुलस्त्यश् च पुलहश् च महातपाः ॥
65.m:
surrounded by all the holy Vidyādharas endowed with yogic perfections,
the Grandfather [Brahmā], Pulastya, and Pulaha of great ascetic austerities,

65.s:
aṅgirāḥ kaśyapo 'triś ca marīcir bhṛgur eva ca
kratur haraḥ pracetāś ca manur dakṣas tathaiva ca //
65.d:
अङ्गिराः कश्यपो ऽत्रिश् च मरीचिर् भृगुर् एव च
क्रतुर् हरः प्रचेताश् च मनुर् दक्षस् तथैव च ॥
65.m:
Aṅgiras, Kaśyapa, Atri, Marīci, and Bhṛgu,
Kratu, Hara, Pracetas, Manu, and likewise Dakṣa,

65.s:
ṛtavaś ca grahāś caiva jyotīṃṣi ca dvijottamāḥ
mūrtimatyaś ca sarito devāś caiva sanātanāḥ //
65.d:
ऋतवश् च ग्रहाश् चैव ज्योतींषि च द्विजोत्तमाः
मूर्तिमत्यश् च सरितो देवाश् चैव सनातनाः ॥
65.m:
and the seasons, the planets, the luminous bodies, O best of twice-borns,
and the rivers in embodied form, and the eternal gods,

65.s:
samudrāś ca hradāś caiva tīrthāni vividhāni ca
pṛthivī dyaur diśaś caiva pādapāś ca dvijottamāḥ //
65.d:
समुद्राश् च ह्रदाश् चैव तीर्थानि विविधानि च
पृथिवी द्यौर् दिशश् चैव पादपाश् च द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
65.m:
oceans, lakes, and various sacred pilgrimage sites,
the earth, sky, directions, and trees, O best of twice-borns,

65.s:
aditir devamātā ca hrīḥ śrīḥ svāhā sarasvatī
umā śacī sinīvālī tathā cānumatiḥ kuhūḥ //
65.d:
अदितिर् देवमाता च ह्रीः श्रीः स्वाहा सरस्वती
उमा शची सिनीवाली तथा चानुमतिः कुहूः ॥
65.m:
Aditi the mother of the gods, Hrī, Śrī, Svāhā, Sarasvatī,
Umā, Śacī, Sinīvālī, and Anumati, and Kuhū,

65.s:
rākā ca dhiṣaṇā caiva patnyaś cānyā divaukasām
himavāṃś caiva vindhyaś ca meruś cānekaśṛṅgavān //
65.d:
राका च धिषणा चैव पत्न्यश् चान्या दिवौकसाम्
हिमवांश् चैव विन्ध्यश् च मेरुश् चानेकशृङ्गवान् ॥
65.m:
Rākā, Dhiṣaṇā, and the other wives of the dwellers in heaven,
Himavat, Vindhya, and Meru of many peaks,

65.s:
airāvataḥ sānucaraḥ kalākāṣṭhās tathaiva ca
māsārdhaṃ māsa-ṛtavas tathā rātryahanī samāḥ //
65.d:
ऐरावतः सानुचरः कलाकाष्ठास् तथैव च
मासार्धं मास-ऋतवस् तथा रात्र्यहनी समाः ॥
65.m:
Airāvata with his attendants, and likewise the measures of time from kalās and kāṣṭhās,
half-months, months, seasons, as well as nights, days, and years,

65.s:
uccaiḥśravā hayaśreṣṭho nāgarājaś ca vāmanaḥ
aruṇo garuḍaś caiva vṛkṣāś cauṣadhibhiḥ saha //
65.d:
उच्चैःश्रवा हयश्रेष्ठो नागराजश् च वामनः
अरुणो गरुडश् चैव वृक्षाश् चौषधिभिः सह ॥
65.m:
Uccaiḥśravas the best of steeds, the serpent-king Vāmana,
Aruṇa, and Garuḍa, and the trees along with medicinal herbs,

65.s:
dharmaś ca bhagavān devaḥ samājagmur hi saṃgatāḥ
kālo yamaś ca mṛtyuś ca yamasyānucarāś ca ye //
65.d:
धर्मश् च भगवान् देवः समाजग्मुर् हि संगताः
कालो यमश् च मृत्युश् च यमस्यानुचराश् च ये ॥
65.m:
and the divine Lord Dharma indeed assembled together;
Time, Yama, Death, and the attendants of Yama,

65.s:
bahulatvāc ca noktā ye vividhā devatāgaṇāḥ
te devasyābhiṣekārthaṃ samāyānti tatas tataḥ //
65.d:
बहुलत्वाच् च नोक्ता ये विविधा देवतागणाः
ते देवस्याभिषेकार्थं समायान्ति ततस् ततः ॥
65.m:
and the various hosts of deities who are not mentioned due to their abundance—
they arrive from here and there for the consecration of the god.

65.s:
gṛhītvā te tadā viprāḥ sarve devā divaukasaḥ
ābhiṣecanikaṃ dravyaṃ maṅgalāni ca sarvaśaḥ //
65.d:
गृहीत्वा ते तदा विप्राः सर्वे देवा दिवौकसः
आभिषेचनिकं द्रव्यं मङ्गलानि च सर्वशः ॥
65.m:
Then, O brāhmaṇas, all those gods, the dwellers of heaven,
having taken the material for the consecration and auspicious items on all sides,

65.s:
divyasaṃbhārasaṃyuktaiḥ kalaśaiḥ kāñcanair dvijāḥ
sārasvatībhiḥ puṇyābhir divyatoyābhir eva ca //
65.d:
दिव्यसंभारसंयुक्तैः कलशैः काञ्चनैर् द्विजाः
सारस्वतीभिः पुण्याभिर् दिव्यतोयाभिर् एव च ॥
65.m:
with golden jars furnished with divine provisions, O twice-borns,
with the sacred waters of the Sarasvatī and divine waters,

65.s:
toyenākāśagaṅgāyāḥ kṛṣṇaṃ rāmeṇa saṃgatam
sapuṣpaiḥ kāñcanaiḥ kumbhaiḥ snāpayanty avanisthitāḥ //
65.d:
तोयेनाकाशगङ्गायाः कृष्णं रामेण संगतम्
सपुष्पैः काञ्चनैः कुम्भैः स्नापयन्त्य् अवनिस्थिताः ॥
65.m:
and with the water of the heavenly Gaṅgā, they bathe Kṛṣṇa joined with Rāma,
standing upon the earth, using golden pitchers mixed with flowers.

65.s:
saṃcaranti vimānāni devānām ambare tathā
uccāvacāni divyāni kāmagāni sthirāṇi ca //
65.d:
संचरन्ति विमानानि देवानाम् अम्बरे तथा
उच्चावचानि दिव्यानि कामगानि स्थिराणि च ॥
65.m:
Then celestial chariots of the gods move about in the sky,
of various kinds, divine, moving at will, and steady,

65.s:
divyaratnavicitrāṇi sevitāny apsarogaṇaiḥ
gītair vādyaiḥ patākābhiḥ śobhitāni samantataḥ //
65.d:
दिव्यरत्नविचित्राणि सेवितान्य् अप्सरोगणैः
गीतैर् वाद्यैः पताकाभिः शोभितानि समन्ततः ॥
65.m:
variegated with divine jewels, frequented by groups of Apsarases,
and adorned all around with songs, musical instruments, and banners.

65.s:
evaṃ tadā muniśreṣṭhāḥ kṛṣṇaṃ rāmeṇa saṃgatam
snāpayitvā subhadrāṃ ca saṃstuvanti mudānvitāḥ //
65.d:
एवं तदा मुनिश्रेष्ठाः कृष्णं रामेण संगतम्
स्नापयित्वा सुभद्रां च संस्तुवन्ति मुदान्विताः ॥
65.m:
Thus then, O best of sages, having bathed Kṛṣṇa joined with Rāma,
and Subhadrā, they praise [them] filled with joy:

65.s:
jaya kṛṣṇa jagannātha jaya saṃkarṣaṇānuja
jaya padmapalāśākṣa jaya vāñchāphalaprada //
65.d:
जय कृष्ण जगन्नाथ जय संकर्षणानुज
जय पद्मपलाशाक्ष जय वाञ्छाफलप्रद ॥
65.m:
"Victory, O Kṛṣṇa, Lord of the Universe! Victory, O younger brother of Saṃkarṣaṇa!
Victory, O lotus-petal-eyed one! Victory, O bestower of the fruits of desires!

65.s:
jaya mālāvṛtoraska jaya cakragadādhara
jaya padmālayākānta jaya viṣṇo namo 'stu te //
65.d:
जय मालावृतोरस्क जय चक्रगदाधर
जय पद्मालयाकान्त जय विष्णो नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
65.m:
Victory, O one whose chest is encircled by garlands! Victory, O holder of the discus and mace!
Victory, O beloved of the one dwelling in a lotus! Victory, O Viṣṇu! Homage be to you!"

65.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ stutvā tadā devāḥ śakrādyā hṛṣṭamānasāḥ
siddhacāraṇasaṃghāś ca ye cānye svargavāsinaḥ //
65.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं स्तुत्वा तदा देवाः शक्राद्या हृष्टमानसाः
सिद्धचारणसंघाश् च ये चान्ये स्वर्गवासिनः ॥
65.m:
Brahmā said:
Having thus praised, then the gods led by Śakra with delighted minds,
and the hosts of Siddhas and Cāraṇas, and whatever other dwellers of heaven,

65.s:
munayo vālakhilyāś ca kṛṣṇaṃ rāmeṇa saṃgatam
subhadrāṃ ca muniśreṣṭhāḥ praṇipatyāmbare sthitāḥ //
65.d:
मुनयो वालखिल्याश् च कृष्णं रामेण संगतम्
सुभद्रां च मुनिश्रेष्ठाः प्रणिपत्याम्बरे स्थिताः ॥
65.m:
the sages, and the Vālakhilyas, having bowed down to Kṛṣṇa joined with Rāma
and to Subhadrā, O best of sages, remained standing in the sky.

65.s:
dṛṣṭvā stutvā namaskṛtvā tadā te tridivaukasaḥ
kṛṣṇaṃ rāmaṃ subhadrāṃ ca yānti svaṃ svaṃ niveśanam //
65.d:
दृष्ट्वा स्तुत्वा नमस्कृत्वा तदा ते त्रिदिवौकसः
कृष्णं रामं सुभद्रां च यान्ति स्वं स्वं निवेशनम् ॥
65.m:
Having gazed upon, praised, and paid homage then to Kṛṣṇa, Rāma, and Subhadrā,
those dwellers of heaven go each to their own abode.

65.s:
saṃcaranti vimānāni devānām ambare tadā
uccāvacāni divyāni kāmagāni sthirāṇi ca //
65.d:
संचरन्ति विमानानि देवानाम् अम्बरे तदा
उच्चावचानि दिव्यानि कामगानि स्थिराणि च ॥
65.m:
Then celestial chariots of the gods move about in the sky,
of various kinds, divine, moving at will, and steady,

65.s:
divyaratnavicitrāṇi sevitāny apsarogaṇaiḥ
gītair vādyaiḥ patākābhiḥ śobhitāni samantataḥ //
65.d:
दिव्यरत्नविचित्राणि सेवितान्य् अप्सरोगणैः
गीतैर् वाद्यैः पताकाभिः शोभितानि समन्ततः ॥
65.m:
variegated with divine jewels, frequented by groups of Apsarases,
and adorned all around with songs, musical instruments, and banners.

65.s:
tasmin kāle tu ye martyāḥ paśyanti puruṣottamam
balabhadraṃ subhadrāṃ ca te yānti padam avyayam //
65.d:
तस्मिन् काले तु ये मर्त्याः पश्यन्ति पुरुषोत्तमम्
बलभद्रं सुभद्रां च ते यान्ति पदम् अव्ययम् ॥
65.m:
Those mortals, however, who at that time see Puruṣottama,
Balabhadra, and Subhadrā, go to the imperishable state.

65.s:
subhadrārāmasahitaṃ mañcasthaṃ puruṣottamam
dṛṣṭvā nirāmayaṃ sthānaṃ yānti nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ //
65.d:
सुभद्रारामसहितं मञ्चस्थं पुरुषोत्तमम्
दृष्ट्वा निरामयं स्थानं यान्ति नास्त्य् अत्र संशयः ॥
65.m: Having beheld Puruṣottama upon the platform, accompanied by Subhadrā and Rāma, / they go to the sorrowless abode; of this there is no doubt.

65.s:
kapilāśatadānena yat phalaṃ puṣkare smṛtam
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mañcasthaṃ sahalāyudham
subhadrāṃ ca muniśreṣṭhāḥ prāpnoti śubhakṛn naraḥ //
65.d:
कपिलाशतदानेन यत् फलं पुष्करे स्मृतम्
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य मञ्चस्थं सहलायुधम्
सुभद्रां च मुनिश्रेष्ठाः प्राप्नोति शुभकृन् नरः ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is remembered [to arise] at Puṣkara from giving a hundred brown cows, / that fruit a man who performs good deeds obtains, O best of sages, / by looking upon Kṛṣṇa upon the platform, together with the plow-armed one and Subhadrā.

65.s:
kanyāśatapradānena yat phalaṃ samudāhṛtam
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mañcasthaṃ labhate naraḥ //
65.d:
कन्याशतप्रदानेन यत् फलं समुदाहृतम्
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य मञ्चस्थं लभते नरः ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is declared [to arise] from giving a hundred maidens, / that fruit a man obtains by looking upon Kṛṣṇa upon the platform.

65.s:
suvarṇaśataniṣkāṇāṃ dānena yat phalaṃ smṛtam
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mañcasthaṃ labhate naraḥ //
65.d:
सुवर्णशतनिष्काणां दानेन यत् फलं स्मृतम्
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य मञ्चस्थं लभते नरः ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is remembered [to arise] from giving a hundred gold coins, / that fruit a man obtains by looking upon Kṛṣṇa upon the platform.

65.s:
gosahasrapradānena yat phalaṃ parikīrtitam
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mañcasthaṃ labhate naraḥ //
65.d:
गोसहस्रप्रदानेन यत् फलं परिकीर्तितम्
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य मञ्चस्थं लभते नरः ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is proclaimed [to arise] from giving a thousand cattle, / that fruit a man obtains by looking upon Kṛṣṇa upon the platform.

65.s:
bhūmidānena vidhivad yat phalaṃ samudāhṛtam
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mañcasthaṃ labhate naraḥ //
65.d:
भूमिदानेन विधिवद् यत् फलं समुदाहृतम्
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य मञ्चस्थं लभते नरः ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is declared [to arise] from the gift of land according to rule, / that fruit a man obtains by looking upon Kṛṣṇa upon the platform.

65.s:
yat phalaṃ cānnadānena arghātithyena kīrtitam
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mañcasthaṃ labhate naraḥ //
65.d:
यत् फलं चान्नदानेन अर्घातिथ्येन कीर्तितम्
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य मञ्चस्थं लभते नरः ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is proclaimed [to arise] from giving food and offering guest-hospitality, / that fruit a man obtains by looking upon Kṛṣṇa upon the platform.

65.s:
vṛṣotsargeṇa vidhivad yat phalaṃ samudāhṛtam
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mañcasthaṃ labhate naraḥ //
65.d:
वृषोत्सर्गेण विधिवद् यत् फलं समुदाहृतम्
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य मञ्चस्थं लभते नरः ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is declared [to arise] from the setting free of a bull according to rule, / that fruit a man obtains by looking upon Kṛṣṇa upon the platform.

65.s:
yat phalaṃ toyadānena grīṣme vānyatra kīrtitam
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mañcasthaṃ labhate naraḥ //
65.d:
यत् फलं तोयदानेन ग्रीष्मे वान्यत्र कीर्तितम्
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य मञ्चस्थं लभते नरः ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is proclaimed [to arise] from giving water in summer or at other times, / that fruit a man obtains by looking upon Kṛṣṇa upon the platform.

65.s:
tiladhenupradānena yat phalaṃ saṃprakīrtitam
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mañcasthaṃ labhate naraḥ //
65.d:
तिलधेनुप्रदानेन यत् फलं संप्रकीर्तितम्
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य मञ्चस्थं लभते नरः ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is celebrated [to arise] from the gift of a cow made of sesame seeds, / that fruit a man obtains by looking upon Kṛṣṇa upon the platform.

65.s:
gajāśvarathadānena yat phalaṃ samudāhṛtam
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mañcasthaṃ labhate naraḥ //
65.d:
गजाश्वरथदानेन यत् फलं समुदाहृतम्
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य मञ्चस्थं लभते नरः ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is declared [to arise] from the gift of elephants, horses, and chariots, / that fruit a man obtains by looking upon Kṛṣṇa upon the platform.

65.s:
suvarṇaśṛṅgīdānena yat phalaṃ samudāhṛtam
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mañcasthaṃ labhate naraḥ //
65.d:
सुवर्णशृङ्गीदानेन यत् फलं समुदाहृतम्
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य मञ्चस्थं लभते नरः ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is declared [to arise] from the gift of a golden-horned cow, / that fruit a man obtains by looking upon Kṛṣṇa upon the platform.

65.s:
jaladhenupradānena yat phalaṃ samudāhṛtam
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mañcasthaṃ labhate naraḥ //
65.d:
जलधेनुप्रदानेन यत् फलं समुदाहृतम्
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य मञ्चस्थं लभते नरः ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is declared [to arise] from the gift of a water-cow, / that fruit a man obtains by looking upon Kṛṣṇa upon the platform.

65.s:
dānena ghṛtadhenvāś ca phalaṃ yat samudāhṛtam
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mañcasthaṃ labhate naraḥ //
65.d:
दानेन घृतधेन्वाश् च फलं यत् समुदाहृतम्
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य मञ्चस्थं लभते नरः ॥
65.m: And whatever fruit is declared [to arise] from the gift of a ghee-cow, / that fruit a man obtains by looking upon Kṛṣṇa upon the platform.

65.s:
cāndrāyaṇena cīrṇena yat phalaṃ samudāhṛtam
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mañcasthaṃ labhate naraḥ //
65.d:
चान्द्रायणेन चीर्णेन यत् फलं समुदाहृतम्
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य मञ्चस्थं लभते नरः ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is declared [to arise] from performing the cāndrāyaṇa penance, / that fruit a man obtains by looking upon Kṛṣṇa upon the platform.

65.s:
māsopavāsair vidhivad yat phalaṃ samudāhṛtam
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mañcasthaṃ labhate naraḥ //
65.d:
मासोपवासैर् विधिवद् यत् फलं समुदाहृतम्
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य मञ्चस्थं लभते नरः ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is declared [to arise] from month-long fasts according to rule, / that fruit a man obtains by looking upon Kṛṣṇa upon the platform.

65.s:
atha kiṃ bahunoktena bhāṣitena punaḥ punaḥ
tasya devasya māhātmyaṃ mañcasthasya dvijottamāḥ //
65.d:
अथ किं बहुनोक्तेन भाषितेन पुनः पुनः
तस्य देवस्य माहात्म्यं मञ्चस्थस्य द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
65.m: Now, what is the use of repeating much in speech over and over again / regarding the greatness of that god upon the platform, O best of the twice-born?

65.s:
yat phalaṃ sarvatīrtheṣu vratair dānaiś ca kīrtitam
tat phalaṃ kṛṣṇam ālokya mañcasthaṃ sahalāyudham //
65.d:
यत् फलं सर्वतीर्थेषु व्रतैर् दानैश् च कीर्तितम्
तत् फलं कृष्णम् आलोक्य मञ्चस्थं सहलायुधम् ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is proclaimed at all tīrthas through observances and gifts, / that fruit a man who performs good deeds obtains, O best of sages, / by looking upon Kṛṣṇa upon the platform, together with the plow-armed one

65.s:
subhadrāṃ ca muniśreṣṭhāḥ prāpnoti śubhakṛn naraḥ
tasmān naro 'thavā nārī paśyet taṃ puruṣottamam //
65.d:
सुभद्रां च मुनिश्रेष्ठाः प्राप्नोति शुभकृन् नरः
तस्मान् नरो ऽथवा नारी पश्येत् तं पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
65.m: and Subhadrā. / Therefore, a man or a woman should look upon that Puruṣottama.

65.s:
tataḥ samastatīrthānāṃ labhet snānādikaṃ phalam
snānaśeṣeṇa kṛṣṇasya toyenātmābhiṣicyate //
65.d:
ततः समस्ततीर्थानां लभेत् स्नानादिकं फलम्
स्नानशेषेण कृष्णस्य तोयेनात्माभिषिच्यते ॥
65.m: Then one obtains the fruit of bathing and other rites at all tīrthas. / [If] one sprinkles oneself with the remainder of the water from Kṛṣṇa's bath,

65.s:
vandhyā mṛtaprajā yā tu durbhagā grahapīḍitā
rākṣasādyair gṛhītā vā tathā rogaiś ca saṃhatāḥ //
65.d:
वन्ध्या मृतप्रजा या तु दुर्भगा ग्रहपीडिता
राक्षसाद्यैर् गृहीता वा तथा रोगैश् च संहताः ॥
65.m: a woman who is barren, whose children are dead, unfortunate, afflicted by planets, / or seized by rākṣasas and the like, or afflicted by diseases—

65.s:
sadyas tāḥ snānaśeṣeṇa udakenābhiṣecitāḥ
prāpnuvantīpsitān kāmān yān yān vāñchanti cepsitān //
65.d:
सद्यस् ताः स्नानशेषेण उदकेनाभिषेचिताः
प्राप्नुवन्तीप्सितान् कामान् यान् यान् वाञ्छन्ति चेप्सितान् ॥
65.m: immediately upon being sprinkled with that remnant of the bath water, / they obtain their desired wishes, whatever desires they seek.

65.s:
putrārthinī labhet putrān saubhāgyaṃ ca sukhārthinī
rogārtā mucyate rogād dhanaṃ ca dhanakāṅkṣiṇī //
65.d:
पुत्रार्थिनी लभेत् पुत्रान् सौभाग्यं च सुखार्थिनी
रोगार्ता मुच्यते रोगाद् धनं च धनकाङ्क्षिणी ॥
65.m: A woman desiring sons obtains sons, and one desiring happiness obtains good fortune; / a woman afflicted with disease is freed from disease, and one longing for wealth [obtains] wealth.

65.s:
puṇyāni yāni toyāni tiṣṭhanti dharaṇītale
tāni snānāvaśeṣasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm //
65.d:
पुण्यानि यानि तोयानि तिष्ठन्ति धरणीतले
तानि स्नानावशेषस्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम् ॥
65.m: Whatever holy waters exist on the surface of the earth, / they are not worth a sixteenth part of that bath remnant.

65.s:
tasmāt snānāvaśeṣaṃ yat kṛṣṇasya salilaṃ dvijāḥ
tenābhiṣiñced gātrāṇi sarvakāmapradaṃ hi tat //
65.d:
तस्मात् स्नानावशेषं यत् कृष्णस्य सलिलं द्विजाः
तेनाभिषिञ्चेद् गात्राणि सर्वकामप्रदं हि तत् ॥
65.m: Therefore, O twice-born ones, with whatever water is left from Kṛṣṇa's bath, / one should sprinkle one's limbs, for it grants all desires.

65.s:
snātaṃ paśyanti ye kṛṣṇaṃ vrajantaṃ dakṣiṇāmukham
brahmahatyādibhiḥ pāpair mucyante te na saṃśayaḥ //
65.d:
स्नातं पश्यन्ति ये कृष्णं व्रजन्तं दक्षिणामुखम्
ब्रह्महत्यादिभिः पापैर् मुच्यन्ते ते न संशयः ॥
65.m: Those who see Kṛṣṇa after his bath, moving southward, / are freed from sins such as killing a brāhmaṇa, without doubt.

65.s:
śāstreṣu yat phalaṃ proktaṃ pṛthiv-yas tripradakṣiṇaiḥ
dṛṣṭvā naro labhet kṛṣṇaṃ vrajantaṃ dakṣiṇāmukham //
65.d:
शास्त्रेषु यत् फलं प्रोक्तं पृथिव्-यस् त्रिप्रदक्षिणैः
दृष्ट्वा नरो लभेत् कृष्णं व्रजन्तं दक्षिणामुखम् ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is declared in the scriptures from three circumambulations of the earth, / a man obtains that fruit by seeing Kṛṣṇa moving southward.

65.s:
tīrthayātrāphalaṃ yat tu pṛthivyāṃ samudāhṛtam
dṛṣṭvā naro labhet kṛṣṇaṃ tat phalaṃ dakṣiṇāmukham //
65.d:
तीर्थयात्राफलं यत् तु पृथिव्यां समुदाहृतम्
दृष्ट्वा नरो लभेत् कृष्णं तत् फलं दक्षिणामुखम् ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit of pilgrimage to tīrthas is declared on earth, / a man obtains that fruit by seeing Kṛṣṇa facing south.

65.s:
badaryāṃ yat phalaṃ proktaṃ dṛṣṭvā nārāyaṇaṃ naram
dṛṣṭvā naro labhet kṛṣṇaṃ tat phalaṃ dakṣiṇāmukham //
65.d:
बदर्यां यत् फलं प्रोक्तं दृष्ट्वा नारायणं नरम्
दृष्ट्वा नरो लभेत् कृष्णं तत् फलं दक्षिणामुखम् ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is declared from seeing Nārāyaṇa and Nara at Badarī, / a man obtains that fruit by seeing Kṛṣṇa facing south.

65.s:
gaṅgādvāre kurukṣetre snānadānena yat phalam
dṛṣṭvā naro labhet kṛṣṇaṃ tat phalaṃ dakṣiṇāmukham //
65.d:
गङ्गाद्वारे कुरुक्षेत्रे स्नानदानेन यत् फलम्
दृष्ट्वा नरो लभेत् कृष्णं तत् फलं दक्षिणामुखम् ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit [arises] from bathing and giving gifts at Gaṅgādvāra and Kurukṣetra, / a man obtains that fruit by seeing Kṛṣṇa facing south.

65.s:
prayāge ca mahāmāghyāṃ yat phalaṃ samudāhṛtam
dṛṣṭvā naro labhet kṛṣṇaṃ tat phalaṃ dakṣiṇāmukham //
65.d:
प्रयागे च महामाघ्यां यत् फलं समुदाहृतम्
दृष्ट्वा नरो लभेत् कृष्णं तत् फलं दक्षिणामुखम् ॥
65.m: And whatever fruit is declared at Prayāga on the great Māgha full moon, / a man obtains that fruit by seeing Kṛṣṇa facing south.

65.s:
śālagrāme mahācaitryāṃ snānadānena yat phalam
dṛṣṭvā naro labhet kṛṣṇaṃ tat phalaṃ dakṣiṇāmukham //
65.d:
शालग्रामे महाचैत्र्यां स्नानदानेन यत् फलम्
दृष्ट्वा नरो लभेत् कृष्णं तत् फलं दक्षिणामुखम् ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit [arises] from bathing and giving gifts at Śālagrāma on the great Caitra full moon, / a man obtains that fruit by seeing Kṛṣṇa facing south.

65.s:
mahābhidhānakārttikyāṃ puṣkare yat phalaṃ smṛtam
dṛṣṭvā naro labhet kṛṣṇaṃ tat phalaṃ dakṣiṇāmukham //
65.d:
महाभिधानकार्त्तिक्यां पुष्करे यत् फलं स्मृतम्
दृष्ट्वा नरो लभेत् कृष्णं तत् फलं दक्षिणामुखम् ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit is remembered at Puṣkara on the celebrated Kārttika full moon, / a man obtains that fruit by seeing Kṛṣṇa facing south.

65.s:
yat phalaṃ snānadānena gaṅgāsāgarasaṃgame
dṛṣṭvā naro labhet kṛṣṇaṃ tat phalaṃ dakṣiṇāmukham //
65.d:
यत् फलं स्नानदानेन गङ्गासागरसंगमे
दृष्ट्वा नरो लभेत् कृष्णं तत् फलं दक्षिणामुखम् ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit [arises] from bathing and giving gifts at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean, / a man obtains that fruit by seeing Kṛṣṇa facing south.

65.s:
graste sūrye kurukṣetre snānadānena yat phalam
dṛṣṭvā naro labhet kṛṣṇaṃ tat phalaṃ dakṣiṇāmukham //
65.d:
ग्रस्ते सूर्ये कुरुक्षेत्रे स्नानदानेन यत् फलम्
दृष्ट्वा नरो लभेत् कृष्णं तत् फलं दक्षिणामुखम् ॥
65.m: Whatever fruit [arises] from bathing and giving gifts at Kurukṣetra when the sun is eclipsed, / a man obtains that fruit by seeing Kṛṣṇa facing south.

65.s:
gaṅgāyāṃ sarvatīrtheṣu yāmuneṣu ca bho dvijāḥ
sārasvateṣu tīrtheṣu tathānyeṣu saraḥsu ca //
65.d:
गङ्गायां सर्वतीर्थेषु यामुनेषु च भो द्विजाः
सारस्वतेषु तीर्थेषु तथान्येषु सरःसु च ॥
65.m: In the Gaṅgā, in all tīrthas, in those of the Yamunā, O twice-born ones, / in the tīrthas of the Sarasvatī, and likewise in other lakes,

65.s:
yat phalaṃ snānadānena vidhivat samudāhṛtam
dṛṣṭvā naro labhet kṛṣṇaṃ tat phalaṃ dakṣiṇāmukham //
65.d:
यत् फलं स्नानदानेन विधिवत् समुदाहृतम्
दृष्ट्वा नरो लभेत् कृष्णं तत् फलं दक्षिणामुखम् ॥
65.m: whatever fruit is declared [to arise] from bathing and giving gifts according to rule, / a man obtains that fruit by seeing Kṛṣṇa facing south.

65.s:
puṣkare cātha tīrtheṣu gaye cāmarakaṇṭake
naimiṣādiṣu tīrtheṣu kṣetreṣv āyataneṣu ca //
65.d:
पुष्करे चाथ तीर्थेषु गये चामरकण्टके
नैमिषादिषु तीर्थेषु क्षेत्रेष्व् आयतनेषु च ॥
65.m: At Puṣkara, and in the tīrthas, at Gayā and at Amarakaṇṭaka, / in tīrthas such as Naimiṣa, and in sacred fields and temples,

65.s:
yat phalaṃ snānadānena rāhugraste divākare
dṛṣṭvā naro labhet kṛṣṇaṃ tat phalaṃ dakṣiṇāmukham //
65.d:
यत् फलं स्नानदानेन राहुग्रस्ते दिवाकरे
दृष्ट्वा नरो लभेत् कृष्णं तत् फलं दक्षिणामुखम् ॥
65.m: whatever fruit [arises] from bathing and giving gifts when the sun is eclipsed by Rāhu, / a man obtains that fruit by seeing Kṛṣṇa facing south.

65.s:
atha kiṃ punar uktena bhāṣitena punaḥ punaḥ
yat kiṃcit kathitaṃ cātra phalaṃ puṇyasya karmaṇaḥ //
65.d:
अथ किं पुनर् उक्तेन भाषितेन पुनः पुनः
यत् किंचित् कथितं चात्र फलं पुण्यस्य कर्मणः ॥
65.m: Now, what is the use of repeating again what has been spoken over and over? / Whatever fruit of meritorious action has been described here,

65.s:
vedaśāstre purāṇe ca bhārate ca dvijottamāḥ
dharmaśāstreṣu sarveṣu tathānyatra manīṣibhiḥ //
65.d:
वेदशास्त्रे पुराणे च भारते च द्विजोत्तमाः
धर्मशास्त्रेषु सर्वेषु तथान्यत्र मनीषिभिः ॥
65.m: in the Veda, the scriptures, the Purāṇa, and the Bhārata, O best of the twice-born, / in all the Dharmaśāstras, and elsewhere by wise sages—

65.s:
dṛṣṭvā naro labhet kṛṣṇaṃ tat phalaṃ sahalāyudham
sakalaṃ bhadrayā sārdhaṃ vrajantaṃ dakṣiṇāmukham //
65.d:
दृष्ट्वा नरो लभेत् कृष्णं तत् फलं सहलायुधम्
सकलं भद्रया सार्धं व्रजन्तं दक्षिणामुखम् ॥
65.m: a man obtains all that fruit by seeing Kṛṣṇa, together with the plow-armed one / and along with Bhadrā, moving southward.

66.s:
brahmovāca
guḍivāmaṇḍapaṃ yāntaṃ ye paśyanti rathe sthitam
kṛṣṇaṃ balaṃ subhadrāṃ ca te yānti bhavanaṃ hareḥ //
66.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
गुडिवामण्डपं यान्तं ये पश्यन्ति रथे स्थितम्
कृष्णं बलं सुभद्रां च ते यान्ति भवनं हरेः ॥
66.m: Brahmā said: / Those who behold Kṛṣṇa, Bala, and Subhadrā standing upon the chariot, / going to the Guḍivā pavilion, go to the abode of Hari.

66.s:
ye paśyanti tadā kṛṣṇaṃ saptāhaṃ maṇḍape sthitam
halinaṃ ca subhadrāṃ ca viṣṇulokaṃ vrajanti te //
66.d:
ये पश्यन्ति तदा कृष्णं सप्ताहं मण्डपे स्थितम्
हलिनं च सुभद्रां च विष्णुलोकं व्रजन्ति ते ॥
66.m: Those who behold Kṛṣṇa, the plow-holder, and Subhadrā / remaining in the pavilion for seven days, go to the world of Viṣṇu.

66.s:
munaya ūcuḥ
kena sā nirmitā yātrā dakṣiṇasyāṃ jagatpate
yātrāphalaṃ ca kiṃ tatra prāpyate brūhi mānavaiḥ //
66.d:
मुनय ऊचुः
केन सा निर्मिता यात्रा दक्षिणस्यां जगत्पते
यात्राफलं च किं तत्र प्राप्यते ब्रूहि मानवैः ॥
66.m: The sages said: / By whom was that procession instituted in the south, O Lord of the World? / And what fruit of the procession is attained there by mortals? Speak!

66.s:
kimarthaṃ sarasas tīre rājñas tasya jagatpate
pavitre vijane deśe gatvā tatra ca maṇḍape //
66.d:
किमर्थं सरसस् तीरे राज्ञस् तस्य जगत्पते
पवित्रे विजने देशे गत्वा तत्र च मण्डपे ॥
66.m: For what reason, on the bank of the lake of that king, O Lord of the World, / did [they], going to a pure, solitary place, and there in the pavilion—

66.s:
kṛṣṇaḥ saṃkarṣaṇaś caiva subhadrā ca rathena te
